```tsx
describe("the Explore list", () => {
  test("its header says how long ago the ranking was computed, or since when it had not been when read, offers Refresh once a newer one is due, and links to How Explore works", () => {
    /** A ranking of the given age, read just now: the answer's Date header and the device's clock agree. */
    const readNow = (age: number): RankingRead => {
      const now = Date.now();
      return { computedAt: new Date(now - age).toISOString(), date: new Date(now).toUTCString(), receivedAt: now };
    };
    // Five seconds past the minute: the Date header counts whole seconds.
    const fresh = html(<ExploreHeader ranking={readNow(3 * 60_000 + 5_000)} onRefresh={() => undefined} />);
    expect(fresh).toContain("Updated 3 minutes ago");
    expect(buttonTag(fresh, "Refresh")).toBe("");
    expect(linkTexts(fresh, "/explore/about")).toEqual(["How Explore works"]);
    const due = html(<ExploreHeader ranking={readNow(6 * 60_000 + 5_000)} onRefresh={() => undefined} />);
    expect(due).toContain("Updated 6 minutes ago");
    expect(buttonTag(due, "Refresh")).not.toBe("");
    const stale = html(<ExploreHeader ranking={readNow(20 * 60_000)} onRefresh={() => undefined} />);
    expect(stale).toContain("Explore has not been updated since ");
    expect(stale).not.toContain("Updated ");
    expect(buttonTag(stale, "Refresh")).not.toBe("");
    // Before the first round there is no ranking, no time to show and nothing to read again.
    const none = html(<ExploreHeader ranking={null} onRefresh={() => undefined} />);
    expect(none).not.toMatch(/Updated|updated since|Refresh/);
    expect(linkTexts(none, "/explore/about")).toEqual(["How Explore works"]);
  });

  test("the ranking's age is its age when read, by the answer's Date header, plus the time on screen; only its age when read makes it stale", () => {
    const computedAt = "2026-09-28T12:00:00.000Z";
    const t0 = Date.parse(computedAt);
    /** The ranking in an answer the server sent `served` ms after computing it, which arrived at the device's `receivedAt`. */
    const ranking = (served: number, receivedAt: number): RankingRead => ({ computedAt, date: new Date(t0 + served).toUTCString(), receivedAt });
    expect(STALE_AFTER_MS).toBe(15 * 60_000);
    // A device clock that agrees with the server's.
    const right = t0 + 190_000;
    expect(rankingAge(ranking(30_000, t0 + 30_000), t0 + 30_000)).toMatchObject({ stale: false, text: "Updated just now" });
    expect(rankingAge(ranking(60_000, t0 + 60_000), t0 + 60_000)).toMatchObject({ stale: false, text: "Updated 1 minute ago" });
    expect(rankingAge(ranking(190_000, right), right)).toMatchObject({ stale: false, text: "Updated 3 minutes ago" });
    // A device clock 20 minutes fast, then one 20 minutes slow: the age at the read is the server's and the time on screen
    // the device's alone, so neither error counts, and neither warns nor calls the ranking new.
    const fast = right + 20 * 60_000;
    expect(rankingAge(ranking(190_000, fast), fast)).toMatchObject({ stale: false, text: "Updated 3 minutes ago" });
    expect(rankingAge(ranking(190_000, fast), fast + 60_000)).toMatchObject({ stale: false, text: "Updated 4 minutes ago" });
    const slow = right - 20 * 60_000;
    expect(rankingAge(ranking(190_000, slow), slow)).toMatchObject({ stale: false, text: "Updated 3 minutes ago" });
    // A page left open counts on, and never turns into the warning: the job has written newer rankings meanwhile.
    expect(rankingAge(ranking(190_000, right), right + 20 * 60_000)).toMatchObject({ stale: false, text: "Updated 23 minutes ago" });
    // Over 15 minutes old when the server answered: by then several rounds have failed or been skipped.
    expect(rankingAge(ranking(15 * 60_000, right), right)).toMatchObject({ stale: false, text: "Updated 15 minutes ago" });
    const stale = rankingAge(ranking(15 * 60_000 + 1000, fast), fast);
    expect(stale.stale).toBe(true);
    expect(stale.text).toMatch(/^Explore has not been updated since .+\.$/);
    expect(stale.text).toContain(new Date(t0).toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit" }));
    // Without a Date header the device's clock is all there is.
    expect(rankingAge({ computedAt, date: null, receivedAt: t0 + 60_000 }, t0 + 60_000)).toMatchObject({ stale: false, text: "Updated 1 minute ago" });
    expect(rankingAge({ computedAt, date: null, receivedAt: t0 + 20 * 60_000 }, t0 + 20 * 60_000)).toMatchObject({ stale: true });
    // The header counts whole seconds, so a ranking of the same second is not in the future; and a minute clock that last
    // ticked before the answer arrived adds no time on screen.
    expect(rankingAge({ computedAt: "2026-09-28T12:00:00.800Z", date: new Date(t0).toUTCString(), receivedAt: right }, right - 30_000)).toMatchObject({
      stale: false,
      text: "Updated just now",
    });
    // Days later the date is named too, so the time cannot be read as today's.
    const old = new Date(t0 - 3 * 24 * 3600_000);
    const days = rankingAge({ computedAt: old.toISOString(), date: new Date(t0).toUTCString(), receivedAt: t0 }, t0);
    expect(days.stale).toBe(true);
    expect(days.text).toContain(old.toLocaleDateString());
  });

  test("Refresh is offered once the ranking on screen is as old as EXPLORE_V1's refresh interval, when a newer one should exist", () => {
    const computedAt = "2026-09-28T12:00:00.000Z";
    const t0 = Date.parse(computedAt);
    // Read a minute after it was computed, then left on screen.
    const read: RankingRead = { computedAt, date: new Date(t0 + 60_000).toUTCString(), receivedAt: t0 + 60_000 };
    expect(EXPLORE_V1.refreshMinutes).toBe(5);
    expect(rankingAge(read, read.receivedAt + 4 * 60_000 - 1000).offerRefresh).toBe(false);
    expect(rankingAge(read, read.receivedAt + 4 * 60_000).offerRefresh).toBe(true);
    // A ranking that was stale when read is offered at once.
    expect(rankingAge({ ...read, date: new Date(t0 + 16 * 60_000).toUTCString() }, read.receivedAt)).toMatchObject({ stale: true, offerRefresh: true });
    // The interval is the formula's.
    const slower: ExploreFormula = { ...EXPLORE_V1, refreshMinutes: 10 };
    expect(rankingAge(read, read.receivedAt + 9 * 60_000 - 1000, slower).offerRefresh).toBe(false);
    expect(rankingAge(read, read.receivedAt + 9 * 60_000, slower).offerRefresh).toBe(true);
  });

  test("a page adds only the posts not on screen; another page is read only while one adds nothing and more follow", () => {
    const shown = new Set([id(1), id(2), id(3)]);
    const some = appendUnseen(shown, explorePage([2, 4, 1, 5], "c1"));
    expect(ids(some.added)).toEqual([id(4), id(5)]);
    expect(some).toMatchObject({ nextCursor: "c1", fetchNext: false });
    expect(appendUnseen(shown, explorePage([3, 1], "c2"))).toEqual({ added: [], nextCursor: "c2", fetchNext: true });
    // The ranking ends.
    expect(appendUnseen(shown, explorePage([2], null))).toEqual({ added: [], nextCursor: null, fetchNext: false });
    // A page whose posts the reader's blocks and mutes all took out is not the end while a cursor follows it.
    expect(appendUnseen(shown, explorePage([], "c3"))).toEqual({ added: [], nextCursor: "c3", fetchNext: true });
    // A post is added once, and the set on screen is left as it was.
    expect(ids(appendUnseen(shown, explorePage([6, 6], null)).added)).toEqual([id(6)]);
    expect([...shown]).toEqual([id(1), id(2), id(3)]);
  });

  /** A fake Explore: each cursor (the first page's is "first") answers a page or an error, and every request is recorded. */
  function fakeExplore(answers: Record<string, ExplorePage | Error>) {
    const calls: (string | undefined)[] = [];
    const fetchPage = async (cursor?: string): Promise<ExplorePage> => {
      calls.push(cursor);
      const answer = answers[cursor ?? "first"];
      if (!answer) throw new Error(`no page for ${cursor ?? "first"}`);
      if (answer instanceof Error) throw answer;
      return answer;
    };
    return { fetchPage, calls };
  }
  const refreshed = () => new ApiError(409, "explore_refreshed", "Explore was refreshed.");

  test("Load more reads the next page of the ranking being paged", async () => {
    const fake = fakeExplore({ c1: explorePage([3, 4], "c2") });
    const result = await readPages(fake.fetchPage, "c1", new Set([id(1), id(2)]));
    expect(fake.calls).toEqual(["c1"]);
    expect(ids(result.added)).toEqual([id(3), id(4)]);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ nextCursor: "c2", refreshed: false });
  });

  test("when the ranking being paged is gone, the new one is read from its first page, keeping only unseen posts, until a page adds some", async () => {
    const fake = fakeExplore({ c2: refreshed(), first: explorePage([2, 1], "n1"), n1: explorePage([1, 5, 2, 6], "n2") });
    const result = await readPages(fake.fetchPage, "c2", new Set([id(1), id(2), id(3)]));
    expect(fake.calls).toEqual(["c2", undefined, "n1"]);
    expect(ids(result.added)).toEqual([id(5), id(6)]);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ nextCursor: "n2", refreshed: true });
    expect(result.last?.computedAt).toBe(AT);
  });

  test("... or until the new ranking ends", async () => {
    const fake = fakeExplore({ c2: refreshed(), first: explorePage([2, 1], "n1"), n1: explorePage([3], null) });
    const result = await readPages(fake.fetchPage, "c2", new Set([id(1), id(2), id(3)]));
    expect(fake.calls).toEqual(["c2", undefined, "n1"]);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ added: [], nextCursor: null, refreshed: true });
  });

  test("any other failure is the list's to show, a first page is never a refresh, and one read is bounded", async () => {
    const failing = fakeExplore({ c1: new ApiError(500, "internal", "Something went wrong on our side. Try again.") });
    await expect(readPages(failing.fetchPage, "c1", new Set())).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: "internal" });
    // Only a cursor names a ranking: the first page is always the current one.
    const first = fakeExplore({ first: refreshed() });
    await expect(readPages(first.fetchPage, undefined, new Set())).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: "explore_refreshed" });
    expect(first.calls).toEqual([undefined]);
    const empty = fakeExplore({ first: explorePage([], "x"), x: explorePage([], "x") });
    const result = await readPages(empty.fetchPage, undefined, new Set(), 3);
    expect(empty.calls).toHaveLength(3);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ added: [], nextCursor: "x" });
  });

  test("the footer: a polite status line always in the tree, Load more while the ranking has more, and signed out the sign-in link when more exist", () => {
    expect(EXPLORE_REFRESHED_NOTICE).toBe("Explore was refreshed; the posts below come from the new ranking.");
    const quiet = html(<ExploreFooter cursor={null} signInForMore={false} notice={null} error={null} onLoadMore={() => undefined} />);
    const status = /<div[^>]*role="status"[^>]*>/.exec(quiet)?.[0] ?? "";
    expect(status).toContain('aria-live="polite"');
    // It can take the focus when Load more, which had it, leaves the tree.
    expect(status).toContain('tabindex="-1"');
    expect(quiet).not.toContain("Load more");
    expect(linkTexts(quiet, "/signin")).toEqual([]);
    const after = html(<ExploreFooter cursor="n2" signInForMore={false} notice={EXPLORE_REFRESHED_NOTICE} error={null} onLoadMore={() => undefined} />);
    expect(after).toMatch(/role="status"[^>]*><div[^>]*>Explore was refreshed; the posts below come from the new ranking\.<\/div>/);
    expect(buttonTag(after, "Load more")).not.toBe("");
    const signedOut = html(<ExploreFooter cursor={null} signInForMore notice={null} error={null} onLoadMore={() => undefined} />);
    expect(linkTexts(signedOut, "/signin")).toEqual(["Sign in to see more of Explore"]);
  });

  /** A fake Explore answering its requests in order from `script`, each a page or a failure, and recording each cursor. */
  function scripted(script: (ExploreAnswer | Error)[]) {
    const calls: (string | undefined)[] = [];
    const fetchPage = async (cursor?: string): Promise<ExploreAnswer> => {
      calls.push(cursor);
      const next = script.shift();
      if (!next) throw new Error(`no answer left for ${cursor ?? "first"}`);
      if (next instanceof Error) throw next;
      return next;
    };
    return { fetchPage, calls };
  }

  test("the list's reader lets one read run at a time: a load meanwhile fetches nothing and answers null, and each read answers what the list shows", async () => {
    const calls: (string | undefined)[] = [];
    const held: ((page: ExploreAnswer) => void)[] = [];
    const reader = exploreReader((cursor) => {
      calls.push(cursor);
      return new Promise<ExploreAnswer>((resolve) => held.push(resolve));
    });
    const first = reader.load();
    // Pull to refresh, Refresh or Load more while the first read runs: nothing is fetched and nothing changes on screen.
    expect(await reader.load()).toBeNull();
    expect(await reader.load("c0")).toBeNull();
    expect(calls).toEqual([undefined]);
    held[0]!(answer([1, 2], "c1"));
    const shown = await first;
    expect(ids(shown!.items)).toEqual([id(1), id(2)]);
    expect(shown).toMatchObject({ cursor: "c1", signInForMore: false, refreshed: false });
    // The ranking's time with the Date header and the arrival of the answer that carried it, which the header ages it by.
    expect(shown!.ranking).toEqual({ computedAt: AT, date: DATE, receivedAt: RECEIVED });
    // Once it has answered the next read runs, and a double press of Load more appends its page once.
    const more = reader.load("c1");
    expect(await reader.load("c1")).toBeNull();
    expect(calls).toEqual([undefined, "c1"]);
    held[1]!(answer([3], null));
    expect(await more).toMatchObject({ cursor: null, refreshed: false });
    expect(ids((await more)!.items)).toEqual([id(1), id(2), id(3)]);
  });

  test("after explore_refreshed the reader appends from the current ranking only the posts not already on screen, and goes on from there", async () => {
    const fake = scripted([answer([1, 2], "c1"), refreshed(), answer([2, 1, 5], "n1"), answer([5, 6], null)]);
    const reader = exploreReader(fake.fetchPage);
    await reader.load();
    const after = await reader.load("c1");
    expect(fake.calls).toEqual([undefined, "c1", undefined]);
    // The posts read stay where they are, once each; the new ranking adds what was not on screen, and the list says so.
    expect(ids(after!.items)).toEqual([id(1), id(2), id(5)]);
    expect(after).toMatchObject({ cursor: "n1", refreshed: true });
    // What it added is on screen now as well: a page holding it again adds only the rest.
    const next = await reader.load("n1");
    expect(ids(next!.items)).toEqual([id(1), id(2), id(5), id(6)]);
    expect(next).toMatchObject({ cursor: null, refreshed: false });
  });

  test("a failed read throws, leaves what the list shows as it was and lets the next load run", async () => {
    const offline = () => new ApiError(0, "network", "Cannot reach korbat. Check your connection.");
    const fake = scripted([offline(), answer([1, 2], "c1"), offline(), answer([3], null)]);
    const reader = exploreReader(fake.fetchPage);
    await expect(reader.load()).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: "network" });
    expect(ids((await reader.load())!.items)).toEqual([id(1), id(2)]);
    await expect(reader.load("c1")).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: "network" });
    // Load more again: its page comes below the posts that stayed.
    expect(ids((await reader.load("c1"))!.items)).toEqual([id(1), id(2), id(3)]);
    expect(fake.calls).toEqual([undefined, undefined, "c1", "c1"]);
  });

  test("a load without a cursor starts over: the first page in place of everything on screen, from which Load more goes on", async () => {
    const later = "2026-09-28T12:10:00.000Z";
    const fake = scripted([answer([1, 2], "c1"), answer([3, 4], "c2"), answer([5, 1], "d1", { computedAt: later }), answer([2, 3], null)]);
    const reader = exploreReader(fake.fetchPage);
    await reader.load();
    expect(ids((await reader.load("c1"))!.items)).toEqual([id(1), id(2), id(3), id(4)]);
    const again = await reader.load();
    expect(ids(again!.items)).toEqual([id(5), id(1)]);
    expect(again).toMatchObject({ cursor: "d1", refreshed: false });
    expect(again!.ranking?.computedAt).toBe(later);
    // The posts shown before it are no longer on screen, so a page holding them adds them like any other.
    expect(ids((await reader.load("d1"))!.items)).toEqual([id(5), id(1), id(2), id(3)]);
  });

  test("a post deleted from the list leaves the reader's list too, even while a read is in flight", async () => {
    let release: ((page: ExploreAnswer) => void) | undefined;
    const reader = exploreReader((cursor) => (cursor === undefined ? Promise.resolve(answer([1, 2], "c1")) : new Promise<ExploreAnswer>((resolve) => (release = resolve))));
    await reader.load();
    const more = reader.load("c1");
    expect(ids(reader.remove(id(2)).items)).toEqual([id(1)]);
    release!(answer([3], null));
    expect(ids((await more)!.items)).toEqual([id(1), id(3)]);
  });

  test("the sign-in flag comes from the last page read, and before the first round there is no ranking to age", async () => {
    const fake = scripted([answer([], null, { computedAt: null }), answer([1], null, { signInForMore: true })]);
    const reader = exploreReader(fake.fetchPage);
    expect(await reader.load()).toMatchObject({ items: [], cursor: null, ranking: null, signInForMore: false });
    expect(await reader.load()).toMatchObject({ cursor: null, ranking: { computedAt: AT }, signInForMore: true });
  });

  test("the list shows what one reader of its own answers, reads the first page again from pull to refresh and Refresh, announces a refresh and keeps the focus", () => {
    const list = block(read("components", "social", "ExploreList.tsx"), "ExploreList");
    const at = (code: string): number => {
      const index = list.indexOf(code);
      expect(index, code).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      return index;
    };
    // Made once with the list, so its state lives and ends with it.
    expect(list).toContain("const [reader] = useState(() => exploreReader(social.explore));");
    // An answer is what the list shows; null, while another read runs, changes nothing.
    expect(at("const answer = await reader.load(after);")).toBeLessThan(at("if (!answer) return;"));
    expect(at("if (!answer) return;")).toBeLessThan(at("setShown(answer);"));
    expect(at("setShown(answer);")).toBeLessThan(at("if (answer.refreshed) {"));
    expect(at("if (answer.refreshed) {")).toBeLessThan(at("setNotice(EXPLORE_REFRESHED_NOTICE);"));
    expect(list).toContain("const remove = (id: string) => setShown(reader.remove(id));");
    // Its posts, Load more's cursor, the ranking's time and the sign-in link all come from the answer.
    for (const wire of [
      "data={shown.items}",
      "<ExploreHeader ranking={shown.ranking} onRefresh={() => refresh(true)} lineRef={line} />",
      "onRefresh={() => refresh(false)}",
      "cursor={shown.cursor}",
      "signInForMore={shown.signInForMore}",
      "if (shown.cursor) void load(shown.cursor);",
      "statusRef={footer}",
      // The empty state is an element, with its own links, not a line of text.
      "<ExploreEmpty onShowLatest={onShowLatest} />",
    ]) {
      expect(list, wire).toContain(wire);
    }
    // After a refresh the focus stays at the footer; after the header's Refresh it goes to the line saying how old the
    // ranking now is, since the button leaves the tree once the ranking is fresh.
    expect(list).toContain("if (refreshes > 0 && shown.cursor === null) (footer.current as unknown as { focus?: () => void } | null)?.focus?.();");
    expect(list).toContain("if (lineFocus > 0) (line.current as unknown as { focus?: () => void } | null)?.focus?.();");
  });

  test("the empty state is worded from EXPLORE_V1, links to How Explore works and offers Show Latest", () => {
    expect(exploreEmptyText()).toBe(
      "Nothing to show in Explore right now. A post appears here when at least 3 other accounts, each at least 2 days old, like or repost it in its first 48 hours. Explore is refreshed every 5 minutes.",
    );
    // Every number comes from the formula: another formula words another sentence.
    const other: ExploreFormula = { ...EXPLORE_V1, threshold: 5, engagerMinAgeHours: 72, windowHours: 24, refreshMinutes: 10 };
    expect(exploreEmptyText(other)).toBe(
      "Nothing to show in Explore right now. A post appears here when at least 5 other accounts, each at least 3 days old, like or repost it in its first 24 hours. Explore is refreshed every 10 minutes.",
    );
    expect(exploreEmptyText({ ...EXPLORE_V1, engagerMinAgeHours: 36 })).toContain("each at least 36 hours old");
    expect(exploreEmptyText({ ...EXPLORE_V1, engagerMinAgeHours: 24 })).toContain("each at least 1 day old");
    const out = html(<ExploreEmpty onShowLatest={() => undefined} />);
    expect(out).toContain(exploreEmptyText());
    expect(linkTexts(out, "/explore/about")).toEqual(["How Explore works"]);
    expect(buttonTag(out, "Show Latest")).not.toBe("");
    expect(textOf(html(<ExploreEmpty onShowLatest={() => undefined} formula={other} />))).toContain("at least 5 other accounts");
  });
});

describe("How Explore works", () => {
  test("states every number of the formula from EXPLORE_V1, with the version and the change log", () => {
    const out = textOf(html(<ExploreRules />));
    for (const phrase of [
      "Original posts from the last 48 hours",
      "was at least 2 days old when it liked or reposted",
      "has stood for at least 10 minutes",
      "A post needs at least 3 approving accounts.",
      "divided by (the hours since it was posted + 2) to the power 1.8",
      "Explore holds the 300 posts with the highest scores, with at most 2 posts of one account",
      "A new ranking is computed every 5 minutes, never sooner than 4.5 minutes after the last one.",
      "The newest 2 rankings are kept",
      "Signed out, you see the first 20 posts.",
      "Explore stays empty for about 2 days after it opens",
      "This is version 1 of the formula.",
      "Version 1, 2026-09-28: First version.",
    ]) {
      expect(out, phrase).toContain(phrase);
    }
  });

  test("follows the formula it is given: another formula's numbers, version and change log", () => {
    const other: ExploreFormula = {
      ...EXPLORE_V1,
      version: 2,
      windowHours: 72,
      engagerMinAgeHours: 96,
      standingMinutes: 15,
      threshold: 7,
      gravity: 1.5,
      offsetHours: 3,
      perAuthor: 4,
      listLength: 100,
      refreshMinutes: 10,
      minGapMinutes: 9,
      kept: 3,
      signedOutPage: 10,
      changes: [...EXPLORE_V1.changes, { version: 2, date: "2026-12-01", summary: "A later version." }],
    };
    const out = textOf(html(<ExploreRules formula={other} />));
    for (const phrase of [
      "Original posts from the last 72 hours",
      "was at least 4 days old when it liked or reposted",
      "has stood for at least 15 minutes",
      "A post needs at least 7 approving accounts.",
      "(the hours since it was posted + 3) to the power 1.5",
      "Explore holds the 100 posts with the highest scores, with at most 4 posts of one account",
      "every 10 minutes, never sooner than 9 minutes after the last one",
      "The newest 3 rankings are kept",
      "Signed out, you see the first 10 posts.",
      "Explore stays empty for about 4 days after it opens",
      "This is version 2 of the formula.",
      "Version 1, 2026-09-28: First version.",
      "Version 2, 2026-12-01: A later version.",
    ]) {
      expect(out, phrase).toContain(phrase);
    }
    for (const phrase of ["48 hours", "2 days", "at least 3 approving", "300 posts", "power 1.8", "version 1 of"]) expect(out, phrase).not.toContain(phrase);
  });

  test("says what takes a post out besides the formula, in the design's words", () => {
    const rule = exploreRules().find((section) => section.title === "What else takes a post out");
    expect(rule?.body).toBe(
      "Besides the formula, only these take a post out of Explore: its moderation state, set by a moderator or by the automatic R1 and R2 checks for every list at once; its author's switch or deletion; a block between you and the author in either direction; your mute. No moderator or automatic lever acts on Explore alone.",
    );
    expect(textOf(html(<ExploreRules />))).toContain(rule!.body);
  });

  test("is a public page with the rules under its title", () => {
    session.state = { status: "signed-out" };
    const out = html(<ExploreAbout />);
    expect(out).toMatch(/<h1[^>]*>How Explore works<\/h1>/);
    expect(textOf(out)).toContain("A post needs at least 3 approving accounts.");
    // Nothing on the page asks who is reading: the rules are the same for everyone, signed in or not.
    expect(read("app", "explore", "about.tsx")).not.toMatch(/Redirect|useSession/);
  });
});

describe("Settings > Privacy: Show my posts in Explore", () => {
  const switchTag = (markup: string): string => /<input[^>]*role="switch"[^>]*>/.exec(markup)?.[0] ?? "";
  /** The switch as Privacy shows it: its state from the hook, which reads the session. */
  function SessionSwitch() {
    return <ExploreSwitch {...useExploreSwitch()} />;
  }

  test("is a switch named Show my posts in Explore, whose state is /api/me's", () => {
    session.state = signedIn(true);
    const on = switchTag(html(<SessionSwitch />));
    expect(on).toContain('type="checkbox"');
    expect(on).toContain('aria-label="Show my posts in Explore"');
    expect(on).toContain('checked=""');
    expect(on).not.toContain("disabled");
    session.state = signedIn(false);
    const off = switchTag(html(<SessionSwitch />));
    expect(off).toContain('aria-label="Show my posts in Explore"');
    expect(off).not.toContain("checked");
  });

  test("shows what it is given: the value being saved, disabled while the save runs, and a failed save's error", () => {
    const saving = switchTag(html(<ExploreSwitch on={false} busy error={null} change={async () => undefined} />));
    expect(saving).not.toContain("checked");
    expect(saving).toContain('disabled=""');
    const failed = html(<ExploreSwitch on busy={false} error="Cannot reach korbat. Check your connection." change={async () => undefined} />);
    expect(switchTag(failed)).toContain('checked=""');
    expect(switchTag(failed)).not.toContain("disabled");
    expect(textOf(failed)).toContain("Cannot reach korbat. Check your connection.");
  });

  test("its one sentence says turning it off takes effect at once and turning it back on at the next refresh", () => {
    expect(exploreSwitchText()).toBe(
      "Your public posts can appear in Explore when other accounts like or repost them: turning this off takes them out at once, and turning it back on takes effect at the next refresh, which comes every 5 minutes.",
    );
    expect(exploreSwitchText({ ...EXPLORE_V1, refreshMinutes: 10 })).toContain("at the next refresh, which comes every 10 minutes.");
    session.state = signedIn(true);
    const out = html(<SessionSwitch />);
    expect(out).toContain(exploreSwitchText());
    expect(linkTexts(out, "/explore/about")).toEqual(["How Explore works"]);
  });

  test("its state and its save live in Privacy, above the list that the Blocked and Muted tabs remount, so a tab change during a save loses neither", () => {
    const privacy = read("app", "settings", "privacy.tsx");
    const screen = block(privacy, "Privacy");
    expect(screen).toContain("const explore = useExploreSwitch();");
    expect(screen).toContain("<ExploreSwitch {...explore} />");
    // The list stays keyed by the tab, so the old tab's rows never show with the new tab's Unblock or Unmute.
    expect(screen).toContain("key={tab}");
    // The switch in the list's header only shows what it is given: it has no state a remount could reset.
    expect(block(privacy, "ExploreSwitch")).not.toMatch(/useState|useEffect|useSession/);
  });

  test("saves with POST or DELETE /api/me/explore while disabled, puts the switch back with the error on failure, and then refreshes the session", () => {
    expect(read("lib", "social.ts")).toContain('setShowInExplore: (on: boolean) => api("/api/me/explore", { method: on ? "POST" : "DELETE", schema: ExploreSettingResponse }),');
    const privacy = read("app", "settings", "privacy.tsx");
    expect(privacy).toContain('<Switch accessibilityLabel="Show my posts in Explore" value={on} disabled={busy} onValueChange={(next) => void change(next)}');
    const change = block(privacy, "useExploreSwitch");
    const at = (code: string): number => {
      const index = change.indexOf(code);
      expect(index, code).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      return index;
    };
    expect(at("if (busy) return;")).toBeLessThan(at("setBusy(true);"));
    expect(at("setOn(next);")).toBeLessThan(at("await social.setShowInExplore(next);"));
    expect(at("await social.setShowInExplore(next);")).toBeLessThan(at("await refresh();"));
    expect(at("} catch (err) {")).toBeLessThan(at("setOn(before);"));
    expect(at("setOn(before);")).toBeLessThan(at("setError(errorMessage(err));"));
    expect(at("} finally {")).toBeLessThan(at("setBusy(false);"));
  });
});

describe("the author's status line", () => {
  test("words every status in the formula's words, with EXPLORE_V1's numbers, and nothing for a reply or a quote", () => {
    const expected: Record<ExploreStatusKind, string | null> = {
      reply: null,
      quote: null,
      not_visible: "Not in Explore: posts under review or removed never appear there.",
      hidden_by_author: "Not in Explore: you turned off Show my posts in Explore.",
      listed: "In Explore",
      outside_window: "Not in Explore: posts can appear only in their first 48 hours.",
      no_ranking: "Not in Explore yet: the first ranking has not been computed.",
      new_since_ranking: "Not in Explore yet: it is newer than the current ranking, so the next refresh will consider it.",
      below_threshold:
        "Not in Explore: fewer than 3 approving accounts. Your own likes, accounts under 2 days old and likes from the last 10 minutes do not count.",
      pending: "Not in Explore yet: the next refresh will consider it.",
      author_cap: "Not in Explore: two of your posts rank above it.",
      below_cutoff: "Not in Explore: it ranks below the 300 posts Explore holds.",
    };
    for (const status of ExploreStatusKind.options) expect(exploreStatusText(status), status).toBe(expected[status]);
  });

  test("takes its numbers from the formula", () => {
    const other: ExploreFormula = { ...EXPLORE_V1, threshold: 5, engagerMinAgeHours: 72, standingMinutes: 15, windowHours: 24, perAuthor: 3, listLength: 100 };
    expect(exploreStatusText("below_threshold", other)).toBe(
      "Not in Explore: fewer than 5 approving accounts. Your own likes, accounts under 3 days old and likes from the last 15 minutes do not count.",
    );
    expect(exploreStatusText("author_cap", other)).toBe("Not in Explore: three of your posts rank above it.");
    expect(exploreStatusText("author_cap", { ...EXPLORE_V1, perAuthor: 1 })).toBe("Not in Explore: one of your posts ranks above it.");
    expect(exploreStatusText("below_cutoff", other)).toBe("Not in Explore: it ranks below the 100 posts Explore holds.");
    expect(exploreStatusText("outside_window", other)).toBe("Not in Explore: posts can appear only in their first 24 hours.");
  });

  test("shows under the author's own top-level post only, never a reply's or a quote's, with links to How Explore works and to the switch", () => {
    const thread = read("app", "post", "[id].tsx");
    expect(thread).toContain("{mine && thread.post.replyTo === null && thread.post.quoteOf === null ? <ExploreStatusLine id={thread.post.id} /> : null}");
    expect(thread).toContain(".exploreStatus(id)");
    expect(thread).toContain("exploreStatusText(answer.status)");
    const line = block(thread, "ExploreStatusLine");
    expect(line).toContain('<Link href="/explore/about" asChild>');
    expect(line).toContain('<Link href="/settings/privacy" asChild>');
    expect(read("lib", "social.ts")).toContain("exploreStatus: (id: string) => api(`${postPath(id)}/explore`, { schema: ExploreStatus }),");
  });

  test("the line and the post are read again whenever the screen gains focus, so both follow a change of the switch made through the line's own link", () => {
    // The web keeps the post's screen mounted under Settings > Privacy, and Back shows that same screen again.
    const thread = read("app", "post", "[id].tsx");
    expect(thread).toContain('import { Link, router, useFocusEffect, useLocalSearchParams } from "expo-router";');
    // The line asks on every focus, as the sign-in screen's autofill starts on every focus, not once per post.
    const line = block(thread, "ExploreStatusLine");
    expect(line).toMatch(/useFocusEffect\(\s+useCallback\(\(\) => \{[\s\S]*?\.exploreStatus\(id\)[\s\S]*?\}, \[id\]\),\s+\);/);
    expect(line).not.toContain("useEffect(");
    // Another post's line never shows under this one while this one's is read.
    expect(line).toContain("const text = line?.id === id ? line.text : null;");
    // The screen reads its post again on every focus after the first, into the thread on screen and without clearing it,
    // so the card's In Explore chip follows; the first focus is the mount, whose read is the thread's own.

describe("no screen caches or stores Explore's answers", () => {

    const callers = sourceFiles().filter((file) => /social\s*\.(explore|popular|exploreStatus)\b/.test(file.text));
    expect(callers.map((file) => file.name).sort()).toEqual(["app/post/[id].tsx", "components/PopularNow.tsx", "components/social/ExploreList.tsx"]);
    const explore = sourceFiles().filter((file) => [...callers.map((caller) => caller.name), "lib/explore.ts", "app/explore/about.tsx"].includes(file.name));

      expect(file.text, file.name).not.toMatch(/^(export )?(let|var) /m);
      expect(file.text, file.name).not.toMatch(/^(export )?const \w+ = new (Map|Set|WeakMap)\b/m);
    }
    // What the app keeps in the browser is the device id and the passkey card's Not now, nothing else.
    const stores = sourceFiles().filter((file) => /localStorage|sessionStorage|indexedDB|AsyncStorage/.test(file.text));
    expect(stores.map((file) => file.name).sort()).toEqual(["lib/api.ts", "lib/passkeys.ts"]);
    // Explore's requests are the client's plain calls, which the API answers no-store.
    const social = read("lib", "social.ts");
    for (const line of social.split("\n").filter((text) => text.includes("/api/timeline/explore") || text.includes("/explore`"))) expect(line).not.toMatch(/cache/i);
  });
});
```

```tsx
import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { cloneElement, type ReactElement } from "react";
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from "react-dom/server";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";
import { ReauthResponse, type MeResponse, type PasskeyView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import EmailRevert from "../src/app/email-revert/[token]";
import NotMe from "../src/app/not-me/[token]";
import PasskeyRemove from "../src/app/passkey-remove/[token]";
import { AddPasskeyDialog, PasskeyItem } from "../src/components/security/PasskeysSection";
import { methodsForLevel, panelStart, REENROLL_HINT, ReauthPanel, reauthNeeded, recoveryCodeSpent, ReenrollNotice, type Method } from "../src/components/security/ReauthPanel";
import { ApiError, apiResponse, messageFor } from "../src/lib/api";
import { AUTOFILL_RESTART_MS, createAutofillScheduler, SUGGESTION_SNOOZE_MS, suggestPasskey, type AutofillEffects } from "../src/lib/passkeys";
import { TERMS_SECTIONS } from "../src/lib/terms";

/**
 * The passkey screens (1c design, section 9): the sign-in autofill's schedule, the level-2 panel's choice, the home
 * card's rule and the messages are pure helpers and are called; the Security list's rows, the Add dialog and the
 * re-authentication panel are server-rendered as lifecycle.test.tsx renders the email-revert page; what a static
 * render cannot show (the sign-in screen's field and button, the pages' calls, the absence of the Signal API) is
 * read from the source, as a11y.test.tsx does.
 */
const SRC = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "src");

/** The route parameters the page under test reads; each test sets them. */
const route = vi.hoisted(() => ({ params: {} as Record<string, string> }));

// expo-router cannot load in Node (it reaches React Native's own modules); Link with `asChild` hands the child its
// href, a page reads its route parameters, and nothing navigates in a static render.
vi.mock("expo-router", () => ({
  Link: ({ href, children }: { href: string; children: ReactElement }) => cloneElement(children, { href } as object),
  router: { replace: () => undefined, push: () => undefined, setParams: () => undefined },
  useLocalSearchParams: () => route.params,
  useFocusEffect: () => undefined,
}));
// The panel and the pages read the session only to refresh it after their call; a static render never makes one.
vi.mock("@/lib/session", () => ({ useSession: () => ({ refresh: async () => undefined }) }));

const html = (element: ReactElement): string => renderToStaticMarkup(element);

const read = (...parts: string[]): string => readFileSync(path.join(SRC, ...parts), "utf8");

/** Every source line matching `pattern`, as `file:line`. */
function findInSource(pattern: RegExp): string[] {
  const found: string[] = [];
  for (const file of readdirSync(SRC, { recursive: true, encoding: "utf8" })) {
    if (!file.endsWith(".ts") && !file.endsWith(".tsx")) continue;
    const lines = readFileSync(path.join(SRC, file), "utf8").split("\n");
    lines.forEach((line, index) => {
      if (pattern.test(line)) found.push(`${file.split(path.sep).join("/")}:${index + 1}`);
    });
  }
  return found.sort();
}

const noop = async () => undefined;
const TOKEN = "A".repeat(20) + "b_-".repeat(7) + "z".repeat(2);

/** Effects the scheduler drives, recorded: the runs it started, the aborts it asked for, and the timers it set. */
function fakeEffects() {
  const started: number[] = [];
  let aborts = 0;
  const timers: { callback: () => void; ms: number; cancelled: boolean }[] = [];
  const effects: AutofillEffects = {
    start: (run) => started.push(run),
    abort: () => {
      aborts += 1;
    },
    after: (callback, ms) => {
      const timer = { callback, ms, cancelled: false };
      timers.push(timer);
      return () => {
        timer.cancelled = true;
      };
    },
  };
  return { effects, started, aborts: () => aborts, timers };
}

describe("the sign-in autofill's schedule", () => {
  test("starts one conditional request when the screen is focused, and never a second while it runs", () => {
    const fx = fakeEffects();
    const scheduler = createAutofillScheduler(fx.effects);
    scheduler.focus();
    scheduler.focus();
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1]);
    expect(scheduler.isCurrent(1)).toBe(true);
    // A challenge lives 10 minutes and conditional mediation ignores the ceremony's timeout, so the request is renewed before its challenge expires.
    expect(AUTOFILL_RESTART_MS).toBe(9 * 60 * 1000);
    expect(fx.timers.map((timer) => timer.ms)).toEqual([AUTOFILL_RESTART_MS]);
  });

  test("renews the request after 9 minutes: aborts it and starts another, and the old one's late ending changes nothing", () => {
    const fx = fakeEffects();
    const scheduler = createAutofillScheduler(fx.effects);
    scheduler.focus();
    fx.timers[0]!.callback();
    expect(fx.aborts()).toBe(1);
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1, 2]);
    expect(scheduler.isCurrent(1)).toBe(false);
    expect(scheduler.isCurrent(2)).toBe(true);
    scheduler.ended(1, "expired");
    scheduler.ended(1, "failed");
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1, 2]);
    expect(scheduler.isCurrent(2)).toBe(true);
  });

  test("starts over after the API said the challenge expired, and stops after any other failure or a sign-in until the next focus", () => {
    const fx = fakeEffects();
    const scheduler = createAutofillScheduler(fx.effects);
    scheduler.focus();
    scheduler.ended(1, "expired");
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1, 2]);
    expect(fx.timers[0]!.cancelled).toBe(true);
    scheduler.ended(2, "failed");
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1, 2]);
    expect(scheduler.isCurrent(2)).toBe(false);
    scheduler.focus();
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
    scheduler.ended(3, "done");
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
    expect(fx.timers.every((timer) => timer.cancelled)).toBe(true);
    expect(fx.aborts()).toBe(0);
  });

  test("aborts the request when the screen loses focus, and starts a new one when it is focused again", () => {
    const fx = fakeEffects();
    const scheduler = createAutofillScheduler(fx.effects);
    scheduler.blur();
    expect(fx.aborts()).toBe(0);
    scheduler.focus();
    scheduler.blur();
    expect(fx.aborts()).toBe(1);
    expect(scheduler.isCurrent(1)).toBe(false);
    expect(fx.timers[0]!.cancelled).toBe(true);
    // The aborted request's own ending arrives later and starts nothing while the screen is away.
    scheduler.ended(1, "expired");
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1]);
    scheduler.focus();
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1, 2]);
  });

  test("holds while the button's own request runs: options fetched meanwhile start no ceremony, and it resumes afterwards if still focused", () => {
    const fx = fakeEffects();
    const scheduler = createAutofillScheduler(fx.effects);
    scheduler.focus();
    scheduler.hold();
    expect(fx.aborts()).toBe(1);
    expect(scheduler.isCurrent(1)).toBe(false);
    scheduler.release();
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1, 2]);
    scheduler.hold();
    scheduler.blur();
    scheduler.release();
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1, 2]);
    scheduler.focus();
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1, 2, 3]);
    // A hold with nothing running aborts nothing.
    scheduler.ended(3, "failed");
    scheduler.hold();
    expect(fx.aborts()).toBe(2);
  });

  test("does nothing once it is disposed, whatever comes after", () => {
    const fx = fakeEffects();
    const scheduler = createAutofillScheduler(fx.effects);
    scheduler.focus();
    scheduler.dispose();
    expect(fx.aborts()).toBe(1);
    scheduler.focus();
    scheduler.release();
    scheduler.ended(1, "expired");
    expect(fx.started).toEqual([1]);
    expect(scheduler.isCurrent(1)).toBe(false);
  });
});

    const out = html(<ReauthPanel me={me} pending={{ action: noop, needed: { level: 2, have: ["password"] } }} onClose={() => undefined} />);
    expect(out).toContain("This change needs two factors because two-factor authentication is on.");
    expect(chips(out)).toEqual(["Authenticator code", "Recovery code"]);
    const first = html(<ReauthPanel me={me} pending={{ action: noop, needed: { level: 2, have: ["totp"] } }} onClose={() => undefined} />);
    expect(chips(first)).toEqual(["Password", "Email code"]);
  });

  test("closing the panel never replaces the route, which would mount the screen anew and lose what the action just showed: the hint is a parameter set on the route the screen is on", () => {
    const source = read("components", "security", "ReauthPanel.tsx");
    // A replace builds a route with a new key: the new recovery codes, a setup's QR code and the flow id of a mailed code would go with the old one.
    expect(source).not.toMatch(/router\.(replace|push|navigate)\(/);
    expect(source.match(/router\.setParams\(\{ reenroll: "1" \}\)/g)).toHaveLength(1);
    // Security reads the parameter where it stands and hands it to the two-factor section; Account and Profile show the notice.
    const security = read("app", "settings", "security.tsx");
    expect(security).toContain("useLocalSearchParams<{ reenroll?: string; add?: string }>()");
    expect(security).toContain('reenroll={reenroll === "1"}');
    for (const screen of ["account.tsx", "profile.tsx"]) expect(read("app", "settings", screen), screen).toContain("<ReenrollNotice me={me} />");
  });

  test("on a screen without a two-factor section the hint is a notice with a link to Security, shown when the parameter is set and two-factor is on", () => {
    route.params = { reenroll: "1" };
    const out = html(<ReenrollNotice me={me} />);
    expect(out).toContain(REENROLL_HINT);
    expect(out).toMatch(/<a[^>]*href="\/settings\/security\?reenroll=1"[^>]*>/);
    // One sentence on the three screens: Security's own, which its two-factor section shows.
    expect(REENROLL_HINT).toBe("You used a recovery code. Set up two-factor again to get a fresh set of codes.");
    expect(read("components", "security", "MfaSection.tsx")).toContain(REENROLL_HINT);
    route.params = {};
    expect(html(<ReenrollNotice me={me} />)).toBe("");
    route.params = { reenroll: "0" };
    expect(html(<ReenrollNotice me={me} />)).toBe("");
    // Without two-factor there is nothing to set up again, as on Security.
    route.params = { reenroll: "1" };
    expect(html(<ReenrollNotice me={{ ...me, user: { ...me.user, mfaEnabled: false } }} />)).toBe("");
    route.params = {};
  });

  test("a spent recovery code is remembered for the panel's life: whichever answer carried it, and whether or not the action then went through, the panel closes with the hint", () => {
    const spent = (answers: unknown[]): boolean => answers.map((answer) => ReauthResponse.parse(answer)).reduce(recoveryCodeSpent, false);
    // At level 2 with nothing proved in time: the recovery code first, after which the action is refused again, then the password.
    expect(spent([{ level: 1, mustReenrollMfa: true }, { level: 2 }])).toBe(true);
    // The password first, then the recovery code.
    expect(spent([{ level: 1 }, { level: 2, mustReenrollMfa: true }])).toBe(true);
    // A recovery code, after which the action fails for a reason of its own: the panel stays open with the error and closes by Cancel.
    expect(spent([{ level: 2, mustReenrollMfa: true }])).toBe(true);
    // No recovery code, no hint.
    expect(spent([{ level: 1 }, { level: 2 }])).toBe(false);
    expect(spent([{ level: 2, mustReenrollMfa: false }])).toBe(false);
    expect(spent([])).toBe(false);

    const source = read("components", "security", "ReauthPanel.tsx");
    // Held in a ref, which outlives one answer, and read from every answer before the action runs.
    expect(source).toContain("const recoveryUsed = useRef(false);");
    expect(source).toContain("recoveryUsed.current = recoveryCodeSpent(recoveryUsed.current, result);");
    expect(source.indexOf("recoveryUsed.current = recoveryCodeSpent(")).toBeLessThan(source.indexOf("await pending.action();"));
    // Acted on in one place, which both ways out of the panel go through: the action that went through, and Cancel.
    expect(source).toMatch(/function close\(\) \{\s*onClose\(\);\s*if \(recoveryUsed\.current\) router\.setParams\(\{ reenroll: "1" \}\);\s*\}/);
    expect(source).toContain('<Button label="Cancel" onPress={close} tone="secondary" />');
    expect(source.match(/^\s*close\(\);$/gm)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(source).not.toMatch(/onPress=\{onClose\}/);
    expect(source.match(/\bonClose\(\)/g)).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  test("the panel follows the refusal it is answering: when another action's refusal replaces the one it shows, it starts over from what that one needs", () => {
    const available: Method[] = ["password", "totp", "email", "recovery"];
    // A level-2 action refused after the password: the two-factor sentence, and second factors only.
    expect(methodsForLevel({ level: 2, have: ["password"] }, available)).toEqual({ methods: ["totp", "recovery"], missing: "second" });
    expect(panelStart({ level: 2, have: ["password"] }, available)).toEqual({ needed: { level: 2, have: ["password"] }, method: "totp", value: "", flowId: null, error: null });
    // "This wasn't me" or "Sign out everywhere" refused while that panel is open: level 1 with nothing proved in time, so
    // every method the account has, the password and the email code among them, and nothing typed, mailed or refused yet.
    expect(methodsForLevel({ level: 1, have: [] }, available)).toEqual({ methods: available, missing: null });
    expect(panelStart({ level: 1, have: [] }, available)).toEqual({ needed: { level: 1, have: [] }, method: "password", value: "", flowId: null, error: null });

    const source = read("components", "security", "ReauthPanel.tsx");
    // The panel is one instance whatever refusal it shows (the screens give it no key), so it compares the refusal it
    // started from with the one it is given, and starts over when they differ.
    expect(source).toContain("const [asked, setAsked] = useState(pending);");
    const reset = /if \(asked !== pending\) \{([^}]*)\}/.exec(source)?.[1] ?? "";
    for (const line of ["const next = panelStart(pending.needed, available);", "setAsked(pending);", "setNeeded(next.needed);", "setMethod(next.method);", "setValue(next.value);", "setFlowId(next.flowId);", "setError(next.error);"]) {
      expect(reset, line).toContain(line);
    }
    // The focus moves to the panel for every refusal, not only the first.
    expect(source).toMatch(/\.focus\?\.\(\);\s*\}, \[pending\]\);/);
    for (const screen of ["security.tsx", "account.tsx", "profile.tsx"]) {
      expect(read("app", "settings", screen), screen).toContain("{reauth.pending ? <ReauthPanel me={me} pending={reauth.pending} onClose={reauth.clear} /> : null}");
    }
  });
});

describe("the sign-in screen", () => {
  const signin = read("app", "(auth)", "signin.tsx");

  test("the email field carries the autofill pair, and the passkey button sends the response with the device fields the password sign-in sends", () => {
    expect(signin).toContain('const EMAIL_AUTOFILL = "email webauthn" as unknown as TextInputProps["autoComplete"];');
    expect(signin).toMatch(/<Field label="Email" autoComplete=\{EMAIL_AUTOFILL\}/);
    expect(signin).toContain('label="Sign in with a passkey"');
    expect(signin).toContain('api("/api/auth/passkey/signin/verify", { json: { response, deviceId: deviceId(), platform }, schema: SignInResponse })');
    expect(signin).toContain('router.replace("/mfa")');
  });

  test("one controller owns the conditional request: focus and blur drive it, and unmounting disposes of it", () => {
    expect(signin).toContain("createAutofillScheduler(");
    expect(signin).toContain("useFocusEffect(");
    expect(signin).toMatch(/scheduler\.blur\(\)/);
    expect(signin).toMatch(/scheduler\.dispose\(\)/);
    expect(signin).toMatch(/scheduler\.hold\(\)/);
  });

  test("no screen calls the Signal API, which deletes other accounts' passkeys on Safari", () => {
    expect(findInSource(/signalUnknownCredential|signalAllAcceptedCredentials|signalCurrentUserDetails|sendSignal\(/)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe("the pages behind the links", () => {
  /** The opening tag of the button whose text is `label`, or "" when there is none. */
  const buttonTag = (markup: string, label: string): string => {
    const at = markup.indexOf(label);
    const role = at === -1 ? -1 : markup.lastIndexOf('role="button"', at);
    return role === -1 ? "" : markup.slice(markup.lastIndexOf("<", role), markup.indexOf(">", role) + 1);
  };
  // The lockdown reaches from the day before its anchor to the moment it runs, which can be a week later: "since", never "in".
  const LOCKDOWN = /passkeys and two-factor authentication set up since the day before/;
  /** A page before the confirmation and after it: the second render starts from the state the confirmation leaves. */
  const sentences = (source: string): string[] => source.replace(/\s+/g, " ").match(/[^.]*set up (?:since|in) the day before[^.;]*/g) ?? [];

  test("the passkey-remove page explains the lockdown, confirms, and offers the button only with the link's token", () => {
    route.params = { token: TOKEN };
    const out = html(<PasskeyRemove />);
    const label = "Remove the passkey and lock down my account";
    expect(out).toContain(label);
    expect(out).toMatch(/sign(s|ed)? out every session/i);
    expect(out).toMatch(LOCKDOWN);
    expect(buttonTag(out, label)).not.toBe("");
    expect(buttonTag(out, label)).not.toContain('aria-disabled="true"');
    expect(out).not.toContain('role="alert"');
    for (const token of ["", "short", "A".repeat(42) + "/"]) {
      route.params = { token };
      const bad = html(<PasskeyRemove />);
      expect(bad, token).toContain('role="alert"');
      expect(bad, token).toMatch(/link is incomplete/);
      expect(buttonTag(bad, label), token).toContain('aria-disabled="true"');
    }
    const source = read("app", "passkey-remove", "[token].tsx");
    expect(source).toContain('api("/api/auth/passkeys/remove-link", { json: { token } })');
    expect(source).toMatch(/router\.replace\("\/signin"\)/);
  });

  test("the not-me and email-undo pages describe the lockdown: every session out, the password removed, and what was set up since the day before", () => {
    route.params = { token: TOKEN };
    for (const [name, page] of [
      ["not-me", <NotMe />],
      ["email-revert", <EmailRevert />],
    ] as const) {
      const out = html(page);
      expect(out, name).toMatch(/sign(s|ed)? out every session/i);
      expect(out, name).toMatch(/remove (your|any) password/i);
      expect(out, name).toMatch(LOCKDOWN);
    }
  });

  test("every explanation of the lockdown names its reach as it is, before the confirmation and after it: what was set up since the day before, the person's own later additions included", () => {
    const anchors = { "passkey-remove": "it was added", "not-me": "that sign-in", "email-revert": "the change" };
    for (const [page, anchor] of Object.entries(anchors)) {
      const found = sentences(read("app", page, "[token].tsx"));
      // Twice on each page: what confirming will do, and what it did.
      expect(found, page).toHaveLength(2);
      for (const sentence of found) expect(sentence, page).toContain(`passkeys and two-factor authentication set up since the day before ${anchor}`);
    }
    // The dialog behind "This wasn't me", whose passkey can be a week old by then.
    const dialog = sentences(read("components", "security", "PasskeysSection.tsx"));
    expect(dialog).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(dialog[0]).toContain("every passkey and two-factor authentication set up since the day before this passkey was added is removed, including any you set up yourself after it");
    // Nowhere does the app say "in the day before", which names one day of what can be eight.
    expect(findInSource(/in the day before/)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe("the terms", () => {
  test("say what a passkey keeps on the server and that nothing about fingerprints or faces leaves the device", () => {
    const body = TERMS_SECTIONS.find((section) => section.title === "Your data")?.body ?? "";
    expect(body).toMatch(/passkey/);
    expect(body).toMatch(/public key/);
    expect(body).toMatch(/the device that added it/);
    expect(body).toMatch(/fingerprint/);
    expect(body).toMatch(/face/);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

const flow = "a".repeat(43);

/** A minimal well-formed authentication assertion, for the passkey re-authentication variant. */

  id: "q2Xx0w8bRk6nV8yQ0f2mUg",
  rawId: "q2Xx0w8bRk6nV8yQ0f2mUg",
  type: "public-key",
  response: { clientDataJSON: "A".repeat(200), authenticatorData: "A".repeat(50), signature: "A".repeat(96) },
  clientExtensionResults: {},
};

  test("email is trimmed and lowercased, invalid rejected", () => {
    expect(Email.parse("  Alice@Example.COM ")).toBe("alice@example.com");
    expect(Email.safeParse("not-an-email").success).toBe(false);
    expect(Email.safeParse(`${"a".repeat(250)}@x.io`).success).toBe(false);
  });
  test("opaque ids are exactly 43 base64url characters", () => {
    expect(OpaqueId.safeParse(flow).success).toBe(true);
    expect(OpaqueId.safeParse("a".repeat(42)).success).toBe(false);
    expect(OpaqueId.safeParse(`${"a".repeat(42)}=`).success).toBe(false);
  });
  test("device ids are 22 to 64 url-safe characters", () => {
    expect(DeviceId.safeParse("x".repeat(22)).success).toBe(true);
    expect(DeviceId.safeParse("x".repeat(21)).success).toBe(false);
    expect(DeviceId.safeParse("x".repeat(65)).success).toBe(false);
  });
  test("recovery codes are normalised to lowercase base32 groups", () => {
    expect(RecoveryCode.parse(" ABCD-EF23-GH45 ")).toBe("abcd-ef23-gh45");
    expect(RecoveryCode.safeParse("abcd-ef01-gh45").success).toBe(false);
  });
  test("display names reject control characters and more than 50 characters", () => {
    expect(DisplayName.parse("  Ada Lovelace ")).toBe("Ada Lovelace");
    expect(DisplayName.safeParse(`bad${String.fromCharCode(7)}name`).success).toBe(false);
    expect(DisplayName.safeParse("x".repeat(51)).success).toBe(false);
  });
  test("phone numbers are E.164 once spaces, hyphens and parentheses are dropped", () => {
    expect(Phone.parse(" +44 7911 123-456 ")).toBe("+447911123456");
    expect(Phone.parse("+1 (415) 555-0132")).toBe("+14155550132");
    expect(Phone.parse("+1234567")).toBe("+1234567");
    expect(Phone.parse(`+${"9".repeat(15)}`)).toBe(`+${"9".repeat(15)}`);
    // No plus, a leading zero, too short, too long, letters, a plus in the middle.
    for (const bad of ["447911123456", "+0447911123456", "+123456", `+${"9".repeat(16)}`, "+44 7911 ext 12", "44+7911123456", ""]) {
      expect(Phone.safeParse(bad).success, bad).toBe(false);
    }
  });
});

describe("auth requests and responses", () => {
  test("email verify response is discriminated by result", () => {
    expect(EmailVerifyResponse.parse({ result: "signup_required" })).toEqual({ result: "signup_required" });
    expect(EmailVerifyResponse.parse({ result: "mfa_required", mfaTicket: flow }).result).toBe("mfa_required");
    expect(EmailVerifyResponse.safeParse({ result: "session" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(EmailVerifyResponse.parse({ result: "session", mustReenrollMfa: false })).toEqual({ result: "session", mustReenrollMfa: false });
  });
  test("mfa verify takes exactly one of code or recoveryCode", () => {
    expect(MfaVerifyRequest.safeParse({ mfaTicket: flow, code: "123456" }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(MfaVerifyRequest.safeParse({ mfaTicket: flow, recoveryCode: "abcd-ef23-gh45" }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(MfaVerifyRequest.safeParse({ mfaTicket: flow, code: "123456", recoveryCode: "abcd-ef23-gh45" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(MfaVerifyRequest.safeParse({ mfaTicket: flow }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("the reauth answer carries the level reached, the rotated token for native clients and, after a recovery code, the re-enrolment flag", () => {

  test("signup completion needs an ISO calendar date", () => {
    expect(SignupCompleteRequest.safeParse({ flowId: flow, dateOfBirth: "2008-02-29", termsVersion: "draft" }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(SignupCompleteRequest.safeParse({ flowId: flow, dateOfBirth: "29/02/2008", termsVersion: "draft" }).success).toBe(false);
  });
  test("a listed session is named by its handle, a uuid that stays while its token rotates, and never by the token's hash", () => {
    const session = { id: userId, deviceLabel: "Chrome on Windows", platform: "web", createdAt: "2026-09-24T10:00:00.000Z", lastUsedAt: "2026-09-24T10:05:00.000Z", current: true };
    expect(SessionsResponse.parse({ sessions: [session, { ...session, id: "0b0e7c1a-5a53-4f0e-8a3f-2f6f8f5d9c11", platform: "ios", current: false }] }).sessions.map((s) => [s.id, s.current])).toEqual([
      [userId, true],

    expect(SessionInfo.safeParse({ ...session, id: undefined }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(SessionInfo.safeParse({ ...session, platform: "desktop" }).success).toBe(false);
  });
  test("me response carries email, the count of passkeys and a nullable profile", () => {
    const me = {
      user: { id: userId, email: "a@b.io", role: "user", onboarded: false, mfaEnabled: false, hasPassword: false, passkeys: 0 },
      profile: null,
      standing: null,

    expect(MeResponse.parse(me)).toEqual(me);
    // The count decides whether the app offers a passkey re-authentication and the suggestion card (1c design, section 9), so it is never left out.
    expect(MeResponse.parse({ ...me, user: { ...me.user, passkeys: 3 } }).user.passkeys).toBe(3);
    expect(MeResponse.safeParse({ ...me, user: { ...me.user, passkeys: undefined } }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(MeResponse.safeParse({ ...me, user: { ...me.user, passkeys: -1 } }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(MeResponse.safeParse({ ...me, user: { ...me.user, passkeys: 1.5 } }).success).toBe(false);
  });
  test("the own profile in the me response says when the handle last changed, whether the badge is held and whether the account's posts show in Explore", () => {
    const user = { id: userId, email: "a@b.io", role: "user", onboarded: true, mfaEnabled: false, hasPassword: false, passkeys: 0 };
    const profile = { id: userId, handle: "ada", displayName: "Ada", handleChangedAt: null, verified: false, showInExplore: true };
    expect(MeResponse.parse({ user, profile, standing: null })).toEqual({ user, profile, standing: null });
    expect(MeProfile.parse({ ...profile, handleChangedAt: "2026-09-24T10:00:00.000Z", verified: true }).verified).toBe(true);

  test("every documented auth error code exists", () => {
    expect(AuthErrorCode.options).toHaveLength(35);

      expect.arrayContaining(["passkey_invalid", "passkey_unsupported", "passkey_limit", "passkey_suspended", "passkey_not_found", "challenge_expired"]),
    );
  });
});

describe("account lifecycle requests and responses", () => {
  test("an email change starts with an address under the sign-up rules and verifies with a flow id and code", () => {

    expect(EmailChangeStartRequest.safeParse({ email: "not-an-email" }).success).toBe(false);
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import {
  CaseSnapshot,
  CaseDecisionAction,
  CaseView,
  FINDING_CATEGORIES,
  ErasureOverdue,
  FindingRequest,
  FindingResponse,
  IdentityRevealRequest,
  QUEUE_PAGE_SIZE,
  QueuePage,
  QueueQuery,
  RevealResponse,
  SOURCE_LABELS,
  STAFF_TEXT_KINDS,
  STAFF_TEXT_MAX,
  SourceSummary,
  StaffOverview,
  StaffSnapshotTaken,
  StaffTextSaveRequest,
  StaffTextSaved,
  StaffTextsResponse,
  TDB_CATEGORIES,
  reporterLabel,
  snapshotDigest,
  staffTextProblem,
} from "../src/index";

/**
 * The console's requests and answers on cases (3c design, section 10): what a moderator's own finding may say, what a
 * saved text must be, and the shapes the queue, the case and the home screen are parsed with.
 */

const CASE = "3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a";
const POST = "7e2d9a10-6c3b-4f5e-8a21-0d4c7b9e1f36";
const OTHER = "5b0e4a52-3c1d-4f6e-9a8b-7c6d5e4f3a2b";
const HEX = "ab".repeat(32);
const TIME = "2026-10-04T08:15:30.123Z";
/** The seven members of 3e on a ledger row of 3c, where each is null. */
const NO_STANDING_COLUMNS = { days: null, announced: null, basis: null, restsOn: null, earliestStart: null, countsUntil: null, period: null, restedOnBy: null } as const;

describe("FindingRequest", () => {
  const finding = { target: { kind: "post", id: POST }, ground: "rule", ruleId: "R1", category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC" };

  test("a moderator's finding cites a korbat rule, R2 among them, about a post, an account or a korbat link", () => {
    for (const ruleId of ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5", "R6"]) expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ruleId }).success, ruleId).toBe(true);
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, target: { kind: "account", handle: "@Some_one" } }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(FindingRequest.parse({ ...finding, target: { kind: "account", handle: "@Some_one" } }).target).toEqual({ kind: "account", handle: "some_one" });
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, target: { kind: "link", url: "https://korbat.example/post/" + POST } }).success).toBe(true);
  });

  test("it has no other ground than a rule: a finding never alleges illegality and never goes the path that records no sender", () => {
    for (const ground of ["illegal", "csam", "order", "law", ""]) expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ground }).success, ground).toBe(false);
    const { ground: _ground, ...withoutGround } = finding;
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse(withoutGround).success).toBe(false);
    // The members of the other grounds are refused, never ignored.
    for (const extra of [{ explanation: "words" }, { bonaFide: true }, { citedLaw: "a law" }, { keyword: "csam" }, { name: "A" }, { email: "a@b.example" }, { turnstileToken: "t" }]) {
      expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ...extra }).success, Object.keys(extra)[0]).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ruleId: "R7" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, ruleId: null }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("its category is one of the Transparency Database's, but not the one that says a notifier was not sure", () => {
    for (const category of TDB_CATEGORIES) {
      expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, category }).success, category).toBe(category !== "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE");
    }
    expect(FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_MADE_UP" }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("the categories a finding may carry are exported as a list, in the Transparency Database's order, for the console's form: exactly those the request takes", () => {
    expect(FINDING_CATEGORIES).toEqual(TDB_CATEGORIES.filter((category) => category !== "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE"));
    expect(FINDING_CATEGORIES).toHaveLength(TDB_CATEGORIES.length - 1);
    expect(TDB_CATEGORIES.filter((category) => FindingRequest.safeParse({ ...finding, category }).success)).toEqual(FINDING_CATEGORIES);
  });

  test("the answer names the case the finding opened or joined", () => {
    expect(FindingResponse.parse({ caseId: CASE })).toEqual({ caseId: CASE });
    expect(FindingResponse.safeParse({ caseId: "x" }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("a saved text", () => {
  const save = { kind: "note", text: "Art. 18 check: no suspicion", salt: HEX, digest: HEX };

  test("is of one of the seven kinds, the recorded choice not to seal among them, with a 32-byte salt and a digest in lower-case hex", () => {
    expect(STAFF_TEXT_KINDS).toEqual(["facts", "reason", "legal_reference", "review_reason", "reveal_reason", "note", "seal_declined"]);
    for (const kind of STAFF_TEXT_KINDS) expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, kind }).success, kind).toBe(true);
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, kind: "statement" }).success).toBe(false);
    for (const bad of [HEX.toUpperCase(), HEX.slice(2), `${HEX}00`, "", "g".repeat(64)]) {
      expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, salt: bad }).success, `salt ${bad}`).toBe(false);
      expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, digest: bad }).success, `digest ${bad}`).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, caseId: CASE }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("the request's schema lets any text through: what a text must be is the route's to refuse, with a code of its own", () => {
    // A text that is too long or holds a control character is answered text_invalid, not invalid_request.
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, text: "x".repeat(STAFF_TEXT_MAX + 1) }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, text: `a${String.fromCharCode(7)}b` }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(StaffTextSaveRequest.safeParse({ ...save, text: 5 }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("staffTextProblem: a well-formed text of at most 5000 UTF-16 units, with no control character but the line feed and no invisible direction or zero-width character", () => {
    expect(STAFF_TEXT_MAX).toBe(5000);
    const LF = String.fromCharCode(10);
    expect(staffTextProblem(`two${LF}lines`)).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem("")).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem("x".repeat(5000))).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem("x".repeat(5001))).toBe("too_long");
    // An emoji is two units: 2500 of them fit, and one more unit does not.
    const emoji = String.fromCodePoint(0x1f600);
    expect(staffTextProblem(emoji.repeat(2500))).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem(`${emoji.repeat(2500)}x`)).toBe("too_long");
    // Half of a surrogate pair has no UTF-8 bytes.
    expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(0xd83d)}b`)).toBe("malformed");
    expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(0xde00)}`)).toBe("malformed");
    // NUL and every other C0 control but the line feed.
    for (let code = 0; code < 32; code++) {
      expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(code)}b`), `U+${code.toString(16)}`).toBe(code === 10 ? null : "control");
    }
    // The invisible direction and spacing characters the notice texts refuse too; the joiners scripts and emoji need stay.
    for (const code of [0x202a, 0x202e, 0x2066, 0x2069, 0x200b, 0x2060, 0xfeff]) expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(code)}b`), `U+${code.toString(16)}`).toBe("format");
    for (const code of [0x200c, 0x200d]) expect(staffTextProblem(`a${String.fromCharCode(code)}b`), `U+${code.toString(16)}`).toBeNull();
    expect(staffTextProblem(`r${String.fromCharCode(0xe9)}sum${String.fromCharCode(0xe9)}`)).toBeNull();
  });

  test("the answers: the stored text's id and digest, the person's own drafts with their salts, and a snapshot's id and digest, never content", () => {
    expect(StaffTextSaved.parse({ id: CASE, digest: HEX })).toEqual({ id: CASE, digest: HEX });
    const draft = { id: CASE, kind: "facts", text: "The post names a home address.", salt: HEX, digest: HEX, createdAt: TIME };
    expect(StaffTextsResponse.parse({ texts: [draft] }).texts).toEqual([draft]);
    expect(Object.keys(StaffSnapshotTaken.parse({ id: CASE, digest: HEX, body: "content", media: [] }))).toEqual(["id", "digest"]);
  });
});

describe("the reveal", () => {
  test("its request is the confirmed params with the key's assertion, and nothing else", () => {
    const stepUp = { id: "Y3JlZA", rawId: "Y3JlZA", type: "public-key", response: { clientDataJSON: "e30", authenticatorData: "AAAA", signature: "AAAA" }, clientExtensionResults: {} };
    const params = { reasonCategory: "impersonation_claim", reasonDigest: HEX };
    expect(IdentityRevealRequest.safeParse({ ...params, stepUp }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(IdentityRevealRequest.safeParse(params).success).toBe(false);
    expect(IdentityRevealRequest.safeParse({ ...params, stepUp, reason: "free text" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(IdentityRevealRequest.safeParse({ ...params, reasonCategory: "curiosity", stepUp }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("its answer is a reporter's handle or a notifier's given name, or neither when the name was forgotten in between; never an address", () => {
    expect(RevealResponse.parse({ handle: "some_one", name: null })).toEqual({ handle: "some_one", name: null });
    expect(RevealResponse.parse({ handle: null, name: "Ada" })).toEqual({ handle: null, name: "Ada" });
    expect(RevealResponse.parse({ handle: null, name: null })).toEqual({ handle: null, name: null });
    expect(Object.keys(RevealResponse.parse({ handle: null, name: "Ada", email: "ada@example.org" }))).toEqual(["handle", "name"]);
  });
});

describe("a source's summary", () => {
  const reporter = { kind: "reporter", label: "Reporter A", accountAge: "1_to_12_months", itemsFiled: "2_to_9", actedOn: "under_half", answeredUnseen: "none", named: null, contactGiven: null, confirmed: null, suppressed: null, contactLost: false };

  test("names nobody: a letter given per case, bands instead of counts, and for a notifier what was given, never what", () => {
    expect(SourceSummary.safeParse(reporter).success).toBe(true);
    expect(SourceSummary.safeParse({ ...reporter, kind: "notifier", label: SOURCE_LABELS.notifier, accountAge: null, itemsFiled: null, actedOn: null, answeredUnseen: null, named: true, contactGiven: true, confirmed: false, suppressed: false }).success).toBe(true);
    for (const kind of ["anonymous", "staff", "unlinked"] as const) {
      expect(SourceSummary.safeParse({ ...reporter, kind, label: SOURCE_LABELS[kind], accountAge: null, itemsFiled: null, actedOn: null, answeredUnseen: null }).success, kind).toBe(true);
    }
    // Bands only: an exact count is no value of any of them.
    expect(SourceSummary.safeParse({ ...reporter, itemsFiled: "7" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(SourceSummary.safeParse({ ...reporter, actedOn: "0.4" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(SourceSummary.safeParse({ ...reporter, answeredUnseen: "3" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(SourceSummary.safeParse({ ...reporter, accountAge: "3_days" }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("its label is one of the console's own: a reporter's letter or the fixed words of its kind, never a text an answer could choose", () => {
    expect(reporterLabel(0)).toBe("Reporter A");
    expect(reporterLabel(1)).toBe("Reporter B");
    expect(reporterLabel(25)).toBe("Reporter Z");
    expect(reporterLabel(26)).toBe("Reporter AA");
    expect(reporterLabel(27)).toBe("Reporter AB");
    expect(reporterLabel(26 + 26 * 26)).toBe("Reporter AAA");
    for (const label of ["korbat: verified notice from police", "Reporter a", "Reporter", "Reporter A ", "<b>Reporter A</b>", SOURCE_LABELS.staff]) {
      expect(SourceSummary.safeParse({ ...reporter, label }).success, label).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(SourceSummary.safeParse({ ...reporter, kind: "staff", label: "Reporter A" }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});

  const summary = { kind: "anonymous", label: SOURCE_LABELS.anonymous, accountAge: null, itemsFiled: null, actedOn: null, answeredUnseen: null, named: null, contactGiven: null, confirmed: null, suppressed: null, contactLost: false };

        ruleId: null,

        categoryKeyword: null,

        decidedAt: TIME,
        staffHandle: "mod_anna",
        throughSeq: 0,

          { id: CASE, kind: "seal_media", mediaId: null, noEffect: null, inForce: true, reversesActionId: null, liftedBy: null, sealed: { posts: 1, images: 1, deletedPosts: 0, list: [{ postId: POST, createdAt: TIME, images: 1 }] }, ...NO_STANDING_COLUMNS },
```
