import type { MediaAttachment, MediaErrorCode, MediaView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import type { MediaFormat } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { MediaFiles } from "./files";
import type { MediaRepo } from "./repo";

/** The media codes plus the shared ones the module also raises; 3e's account_suspended is the social module's code, shared. */
export type MediaErrorKind = MediaErrorCode | "not_found" | "invalid_request" | "account_suspended";
export type MediaErrorStatus = 400 | 403 | 404 | 409 | 413 | 415 | 503;

const MESSAGES: Record<MediaErrorKind, string> = {
  unsupported_media_type: "That file type is not supported. Use a JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or GIF image.",
  file_too_large: "Images can be at most 20 MB.",
  too_many_pending_uploads: "You have too many images waiting to be posted. Post or remove some first.",
  uploads_unavailable: "Image uploads are temporarily unavailable. Try again later.",
  media_unavailable: "One of the images is not available. Remove it and add it again.",
  not_found: "Not found.",
  invalid_request: "Some details are missing or invalid.",
  // 3e (design, sections 7.2 and 9.8): an upload while the account's suspension runs, in the social module's words.
  account_suspended: "Your account is suspended, so you cannot do this now.",
};

/** What an iPhone calls a photo. The decoder cannot read it, so the message says what to do instead. */
export const HEIC_MESSAGE = "HEIC photos are not supported. Export the photo as JPEG and try again.";

/** An expected, user-facing failure. The HTTP layer turns it into an ErrorEnvelope with this code and status. */
export class MediaError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly code: MediaErrorKind,
    readonly status: MediaErrorStatus,
    message: string = MESSAGES[code],
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "MediaError";
  }
}

export function mediaErrorMessage(code: MediaErrorKind): string {
  return MESSAGES[code];
}

/**
 * An image of a post as this module hands it to the social module, with the image's own moderation state: the view
 * builder decides from the state and the viewer what a reader gets. A sealed image is its id and its state only (3c
 * design, section 7.10): nobody is given its size, its blurhash, its alt text or a path.
 */
export type PostImage = (Omit<MediaView, "moderation"> & { state: "visible" | "withheld" | "removed" }) | { id: string; state: "sealed" };

/**
 * What the social module needs from this one. `attach` and `detachAll` run inside the social
 * module's own transaction; `requestDeletion` runs after it committed, because files cannot be
 * rolled back. `detachAll` answers only the images that are really gone: a row a case holds, and every
 * row of a frozen post, stays, and no deletion may be requested for its files. `forPosts` never lists
 * an image of a deleted post or an erased image.
 */
export interface MediaForPosts {
  attach(tx: DbTx, input: { postId: string; ownerId: string; items: readonly MediaAttachment[] }): Promise<void>;
  detachAll(tx: DbTx, postId: string): Promise<string[]>;
  requestDeletion(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void>;
  forPosts(postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, PostImage[]>>;
}

/** How many uploads one account may hold that are not on a post yet. */
export const MAX_PENDING_UPLOADS = 20;

export interface MediaDeps {
  repo: MediaRepo;
  files: MediaFiles;
  /** The formats MEDIA_FORMATS enables. The worker reads the same setting. */
  formats: readonly MediaFormat[];
  /** Uploads are refused while either volume has less free space than this. */
  minFreeBytes: number;
  /** See MEDIA_RECONCILE. `on` refuses to delete many orphans at once; `force` does not; `off` skips the pass. */
  reconcileMode: "on" | "off" | "force";
  /** Counts one upload against the account's hourly limit and throws when it is used up. */
  enforceUploadLimit: (userId: string, accountCreatedAt: Date, now: Date) => Promise<void>;
  log: Logger;
  now: () => Date;
}

import { and, eq, gt, inArray, isNotNull, isNull, lt, ne, or, sql, type SQL } from "drizzle-orm";
import { mediaPath } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { postMedia, posts, profiles, type Db, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import type { ResultFile } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import { WRITE_CLOCK, liveNotSuspended } from "../lib/standing";
import { MediaError, type PostImage } from "./context";

/**
 * Every SQL statement on post_media lives in this module's repository, on the korbat_api pool, and so does every
 * statement on media_holds, a case's evidence holds on image rows (3c design, section 5).
 *
 * Two rules of the database shape what is written here (3c design, section 6.1). The trigger post_media_keep decides for
 * every delete whether a row goes: it skips a row a hold retains and every row of a frozen post, so no delete below
 * filters for either, and each answers only the ids of the rows that are really gone, which are the only files a caller
 * may ask the worker to delete. And every statement that locks or deletes several image rows takes them in id order, so
 * that no two transactions ever lock one post's images in opposite orders.
 */

export interface MediaRow {
  id: string;
  ownerId: string;
  status: "processing" | "ready" | "failed";
  error: string | null;
  postId: string | null;
  width: number | null;
  height: number | null;
  blurhash: string | null;
  createdAt: Date;
  /** The image's own moderation state, which only a migrator-owned function writes. A sealed image is shown to nobody. */
  moderationState: "visible" | "withheld" | "removed" | "sealed";
}

/** One hold request of an intake: a post whose images the case holds as evidence, or an account whose images are only locked. */
export type HoldPair = { caseId: string; postId: string } | { ownerId: string };

/** An image as a case's snapshot lists it. The alt text is null for an image whose content was erased. */
export interface HeldImage {
  id: string;
  alt: string | null;
  width: number;
  height: number;
}

/** What a case about a post or an account reaches: counts, a day and a time, never an id, an alt text or a file. */
export interface CaseReach {
  /** The posts the case reaches that have image rows. */
  posts: number;
  images: number;
  sealed: number;
  /** The images korbat's server would still give to some reader. */
  served: number;
  /** The creation day, in UTC, of the newest post with image rows. */
  newestPostOn: string | null;
  /** When the newest post with a served image was created. */
  newestServedAt: Date | null;
}

/** Ids as one uuid[] parameter. */
const uuidArray = (ids: readonly string[]): SQL => sql`${`{${ids.join(",")}}`}::uuid[]`;

/**
 * An image the data export hands its owner: ready, in a state its author still sees (a sealed image is exported to
 * nobody, and a state this reader has not been taught is left out), not erased, and either on no post or on a post that
 * is neither deleted nor erased. A row that a case or a freeze kept after its post was deleted is in no export. The
 * query it is used in joins posts by the image's post.
 */
const EXPORTABLE = and(
  eq(postMedia.status, "ready"),
  inArray(postMedia.moderationState, ["visible", "withheld", "removed"]),
  isNull(postMedia.erasedAt),
  or(isNull(postMedia.postId), and(ne(posts.state, "deleted_by_author"), isNull(posts.erasedAt))),
);

/**
 * A row the disposal may take (3c design, section 7.9): nothing retains it (no hold stands, and its post is not frozen),
 * and its post is deleted, its owner is purged, or its post's content or its own was erased. `m` is the image row, `p`
 * its post when it has one, `o` its owner's profile. The freeze is read here only to keep kept rows out of a batch: for
 * each row that is deleted, post_media_keep decides.
 *
 * The marks and the freeze are one condition, a CASE that reads the freeze only for a row that carries a mark. As two
 * conditions the planner made the freeze the filter of the scan of post_media, since it names that table alone, and
 * called it for every attached image row in the table before any mark was tested: several index probes a row, seconds
 * for a table of thousands, however few rows were disposable. A CASE is evaluated in the order it is written, and this
 * one names all three tables, so it runs where they are joined.
 */
const DISPOSABLE = sql`(m.hold_until is null or m.hold_until <= now())
  and case when (p.state = 'deleted_by_author' or o.deleted_at is not null or p.erased_at is not null or m.erased_at is not null)
           then (m.post_id is null or not public.post_frozen(m.post_id))
           else false end`;

const columns = {
  id: postMedia.id,
  ownerId: postMedia.ownerId,
  status: postMedia.status,
  error: postMedia.error,
  postId: postMedia.postId,
  width: postMedia.width,
  height: postMedia.height,
  blurhash: postMedia.blurhash,
  createdAt: postMedia.createdAt,
  moderationState: postMedia.moderationState,
};

export function createMediaRepo(db: Db) {
  return {
    /** When the account was onboarded, which decides its upload tier. */
    async accountCreatedAt(userId: string): Promise<Date | null> {
      const rows = await db.select({ createdAt: profiles.createdAt }).from(profiles).where(eq(profiles.id, userId)).limit(1);
      return rows[0]?.createdAt ?? null;
    },

    /** Uploads of this account that are not on a post yet and did not fail. */
    async pendingCount(ownerId: string): Promise<number> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ count: sql<number>`count(*)::int` })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), isNull(postMedia.postId), inArray(postMedia.status, ["processing", "ready"])));
      return rows[0]?.count ?? 0;
    },

    /**
     * The upload's row, as one statement that locks its owner's profile row FOR KEY SHARE and inserts only when the one
     * predicate holds (3e design, section 7.2): read in the statement that locks the row, by the clock. No row inserted
     * answers account_suspended, and the caller discards the received file.
     */
    async insertProcessing(input: { id: string; ownerId: string; now: Date }): Promise<void> {
      const inserted = await db.execute(sql`
        with ok as (select p.id from profiles p where p.id = ${input.ownerId}::uuid and ${liveNotSuspended("p", WRITE_CLOCK)} for key share of p)
        insert into post_media (id, owner_id, status, created_at)
        select ${input.id}::uuid, ok.id, 'processing', ${input.now.toISOString()}::timestamptz from ok
        returning id`);
      if (inserted.length === 0) throw new MediaError("account_suspended", 403);
    },

    /**
     * One image row, for its owner's status. Two rules of the readers hold here (3c design, section 7.10): a row that a
     * case or a freeze keeps after its post was deleted, and a row whose content, its own or its post's, was erased, is
     * answered as a row that does not exist, to its owner too, so nothing tells the author that the row was kept; and a
     * sealed image is handed over without its blurhash, which is made from the image.
     */
    async find(id: string): Promise<MediaRow | null> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ ...columns, erasedAt: postMedia.erasedAt, postState: posts.state, postErasedAt: posts.erasedAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(eq(postMedia.id, id))
        .limit(1);
      const found = rows[0];
      if (!found || found.postState === "deleted_by_author" || found.erasedAt !== null || found.postErasedAt !== null) return null;
      const { erasedAt: _erasedAt, postState: _postState, postErasedAt: _postErasedAt, ...row } = found;
      return row.moderationState === "sealed" ? { ...row, blurhash: null } : row;
    },

    /** Records the worker's verdict, once. A row that is no longer processing is left as it is. */
    async finalize(id: string, result: ResultFile): Promise<boolean> {
      const values = result.status === "ready" ? { status: "ready" as const, width: result.width, height: result.height, blurhash: result.blurhash } : { status: "failed" as const, error: result.reason };
      const rows = await db.update(postMedia).set(values).where(and(eq(postMedia.id, id), eq(postMedia.status, "processing"))).returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    /** Removes an upload of this account that is not on a post. */
    async deleteUnattached(id: string, ownerId: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db.delete(postMedia).where(and(eq(postMedia.id, id), eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), isNull(postMedia.postId))).returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    /**
     * What serving an image file depends on: whether it is ready, its own moderation state, its post's state and author,
     * and whether its content or its post's was erased.
     */
    async fileAccess(id: string): Promise<{ status: MediaRow["status"]; mediaState: MediaRow["moderationState"]; postState: string | null; authorId: string | null; erased: boolean } | null> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ status: postMedia.status, mediaState: postMedia.moderationState, postState: posts.state, authorId: posts.authorId, erasedAt: postMedia.erasedAt, postErasedAt: posts.erasedAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(eq(postMedia.id, id))
        .limit(1);
      const found = rows[0];
      if (!found) return null;
      return { status: found.status, mediaState: found.mediaState, postState: found.postState, authorId: found.authorId, erased: found.erasedAt !== null || found.postErasedAt !== null };
    },

    /**
     * Puts images on a post, inside the transaction that creates it. Each must belong to the author,
     * be ready and be on no post yet; anything else rolls the post back.
     */
    async attach(tx: DbTx, input: { postId: string; ownerId: string; items: readonly { id: string; alt: string }[] }): Promise<void> {
      for (const [position, item] of input.items.entries()) {
        const rows = await tx
          .update(postMedia)
          .set({ postId: input.postId, position, altText: item.alt })
          .where(and(eq(postMedia.id, item.id), eq(postMedia.ownerId, input.ownerId), isNull(postMedia.postId), eq(postMedia.status, "ready")))
          .returning({ id: postMedia.id });
        if (rows.length !== 1) throw new MediaError("media_unavailable", 400);
      }
    },

    /**
     * Removes a post's images, inside the transaction that deletes it, and says which files to delete afterwards. The
     * rows are taken in id order, under row locks, with no filter of its own: the keep trigger skips every row a case
     * holds and every row of a frozen post, and RETURNING omits them, so no file of a kept row is asked for. A plain
     * delete by post takes the rows in its scan's order, and deadlocked with an intake that locks the same rows by id.
     */
    async detachAll(tx: DbTx, postId: string): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = (await tx.execute(
        sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where post_id = ${postId}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`,
      )) as unknown as { id: string }[];
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Removes every image row of the owner, on a post or not, whatever its state, inside the transaction
     * that purges the account, and says which files to delete afterwards (1b design, section 7.6). In id order under
     * row locks and with no filter, as detachAll: the keep trigger decides which rows stay.
     */
    async purgeOwner(tx: DbTx, ownerId: string): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = (await tx.execute(
        sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where owner_id = ${ownerId}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`,
      )) as unknown as { id: string }[];
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * The images of a page of posts, in one query, in their order on each post, each with its own moderation state:
     * what the state means for a reader is the view builder's to say. A sealed image is its id and its state only:
     * nobody is given its size, its blurhash, its alt text or a path. An image of a deleted post, and one whose content
     * or whose post's was erased, is given to nobody, its owner included, so no view and no export names a row that a
     * case or a freeze kept. A state this reader has not been taught is left out.
     */
    async forPosts(postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, PostImage[]>> {
      const byPost = new Map<string, PostImage[]>();
      if (postIds.length === 0) return byPost;
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id, postId: postMedia.postId, width: postMedia.width, height: postMedia.height, blurhash: postMedia.blurhash, altText: postMedia.altText, state: postMedia.moderationState })
        .from(postMedia)
        .innerJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(and(inArray(postMedia.postId, [...postIds]), eq(postMedia.status, "ready"), ne(posts.state, "deleted_by_author"), isNull(postMedia.erasedAt), isNull(posts.erasedAt)))
        .orderBy(postMedia.postId, postMedia.position);
      for (const row of rows) {
        if (!row.postId) continue;
        let image: PostImage;
        if (row.state === "sealed") image = { id: row.id, state: "sealed" };
        else if (row.state === "visible" || row.state === "withheld" || row.state === "removed") {
          if (row.width === null || row.height === null || row.blurhash === null) continue;
          image = { id: row.id, state: row.state, width: row.width, height: row.height, blurhash: row.blurhash, alt: row.altText ?? "", small: mediaPath(row.id, "small"), large: mediaPath(row.id, "large") };
        } else {
          // A state added later does not compile until this reader says who is given it.
          const unknown: never = row.state;
          void unknown;
          continue;
        }
        byPost.set(row.postId, [...(byPost.get(row.postId) ?? []), image]);
      }
      return byPost;
    },

    /**
     * Every image of the account that the data export takes a file for, on a post or not, oldest first: the ready ones
     * the account still sees (EXPORTABLE). A withheld or removed image stays with its author; a sealed image, an image
     * of a deleted post and an erased one are exported to nobody.
     */
    async readyImages(ownerId: string): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), EXPORTABLE))
        .orderBy(postMedia.createdAt, postMedia.id);
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Whether readyImages would still list this image of the owner: the export reads the row again when it opens each
     * file, so an image that was sealed, erased or deleted with its post while the archive streams is left out of it.
     */
    async isExportable(ownerId: string, id: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.id, id), eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), EXPORTABLE))
        .limit(1);
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    /** Uploads that still wait for the worker's verdict. */
    async processingIds(): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db.select({ id: postMedia.id }).from(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.status, "processing")).orderBy(postMedia.createdAt);
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /** Fails uploads the worker has not answered since `before`, and says which. */
    async failStale(before: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(postMedia)
        .set({ status: "failed", error: "processing_failed" })
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.status, "processing"), lt(postMedia.createdAt, before)))
        .returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /** Removes uploads made before `before` that were never put on a post, whatever their state, and says which. */
    async deleteUnattachedBefore(before: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db.delete(postMedia).where(and(isNull(postMedia.postId), lt(postMedia.createdAt, before))).returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Which of these ids have a row, whatever the row's state: the reconcile pass asks it which stored files belong to
     * no row, so a row that a hold or a freeze keeps must be seen here, or its files would be swept as orphans.
     */
    async existing(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<Set<string>> {
      if (ids.length === 0) return new Set();
      const rows = await db.select({ id: postMedia.id }).from(postMedia).where(inArray(postMedia.id, [...ids]));
      return new Set(rows.map((row) => row.id));
    },

    /** Removes a row whatever its state. Used when an upload could not be handed to the worker. */
    async deleteRow(id: string): Promise<void> {
      await db.delete(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ what moderation cases need

    /**
     * An intake's holds (3c design, sections 5 and 7.1, step 4), inside the intake's transaction. First one statement
     * locks, FOR KEY SHARE and in one id order, every image row the pairs name: the rows of each post and, for an owner
     * pair, every row of that owner that is on a post (an attached row's owner is its post's author, so those are the
     * images of the account's posts). The posts are read there, never locked. The lock is what makes a delete that races
     * the intake wait and then read the intake's committed item; a row whose delete committed first is not returned.
     * Then, for the post pairs only, the case's hold goes on each returned row that has no unreleased hold from that case
     * and is not erased, in id order, which is the order the holds are released in: an owner pair gets no hold, since the
     * images of a frozen post are kept whether a hold stands or not. It answers, for each post pair, the post's images
     * in position order, an erased one without its alt text; an empty list means the images are gone.
     */
    async hold(tx: DbTx, pairs: readonly HoldPair[]): Promise<Map<string, HeldImage[]>> {
      const caseOf = new Map<string, string>();
      const owners: string[] = [];
      for (const pair of pairs) {
        if ("postId" in pair) caseOf.set(pair.postId, pair.caseId);
        else owners.push(pair.ownerId);
      }
      const held = new Map<string, HeldImage[]>([...caseOf.keys()].map((postId) => [postId, []]));
      if (caseOf.size === 0 && owners.length === 0) return held;

      const locked = (await tx.execute(sql`
        select m.id, m.post_id, m.position, m.width, m.height, m.alt_text, (m.erased_at is not null or p.erased_at is not null) as erased
        from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where m.post_id = any(${uuidArray([...caseOf.keys()])}) or m.owner_id = any(${uuidArray(owners)})
        order by m.id for key share of m`)) as unknown as { id: string; post_id: string; position: number; width: number; height: number; alt_text: string | null; erased: boolean }[];

      // The rows came back in id order; the holds are placed in that order too.
      const toHold = locked.filter((row) => caseOf.has(row.post_id) && !row.erased);
      if (toHold.length > 0) {
        await tx.execute(sql`
          insert into media_holds (media_id, case_id)
          select v.media_id, v.case_id
          from unnest(${uuidArray(toHold.map((row) => row.id))}, ${uuidArray(toHold.map((row) => caseOf.get(row.post_id)!))}) as v(media_id, case_id)
          where not exists (select 1 from media_holds h where h.media_id = v.media_id and h.case_id = v.case_id and h.released_at is null)
          order by v.media_id`);
      }

      for (const row of [...locked].sort((a, b) => a.position - b.position)) {
        held.get(row.post_id)?.push({ id: row.id, alt: row.erased ? null : (row.alt_text ?? ""), width: row.width, height: row.height });
      }
      return held;
    },

    /**
     * What a case about this post or this account reaches (3c design, section 6.1): the post itself, or every post
     * whose author is the account, whatever its state. One statement that locks nothing.
     */
    async reach(target: { type: "post" | "account"; id: string }): Promise<CaseReach> {
      const served = sql`m.moderation_state <> 'sealed' and p.state <> 'deleted_by_author' and m.erased_at is null and p.erased_at is null`;
      const reached = target.type === "post" ? sql`m.post_id = ${target.id}::uuid` : sql`p.author_id = ${target.id}::uuid`;
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`
        select count(distinct m.post_id)::int as posts,
               count(*)::int as images,
               (count(*) filter (where m.moderation_state = 'sealed'))::int as sealed,
               (count(*) filter (where ${served}))::int as served,
               to_char(max(p.created_at) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD') as newest_post_on,
               to_char(max(p.created_at) filter (where ${served}) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as newest_served_at
        from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where ${reached}`)) as unknown as { posts: number; images: number; sealed: number; served: number; newest_post_on: string | null; newest_served_at: string | null }[];
      return {
        posts: row!.posts,
        images: row!.images,
        sealed: row!.sealed,
        served: row!.served,
        newestPostOn: row!.newest_post_on,
        newestServedAt: row!.newest_served_at === null ? null : new Date(row!.newest_served_at),
      };
    },

    /**
     * What opening an image for staff depends on, in one query: the row with its post, its size and its own state,
     * whether its content or its post's was erased, and whether its post is frozen now. Null when no row has the id or
     * the image is on no post.
     */
    async staffAccess(id: string): Promise<{ postId: string; status: MediaRow["status"]; width: number | null; height: number | null; mediaState: MediaRow["moderationState"]; erased: boolean; frozen: boolean } | null> {
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`
        select m.post_id, m.status, m.width, m.height, m.moderation_state, (m.erased_at is not null or p.erased_at is not null) as erased, public.post_frozen(m.post_id) as frozen
        from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where m.id = ${id}::uuid`)) as unknown as { post_id: string; status: MediaRow["status"]; width: number | null; height: number | null; moderation_state: MediaRow["moderationState"]; erased: boolean; frozen: boolean }[];
      if (!row) return null;
      return { postId: row.post_id, status: row.status, width: row.width, height: row.height, mediaState: row.moderation_state, erased: row.erased, frozen: row.frozen };
    },

    /**
     * A page of the image rows that are on a post, in id order after `afterId` (from the start when it is null): each
     * one's id, its post, its stored moderation state and when its content was erased. It locks nothing and gives nothing
     * of an image itself. The staff command line's text-verify reads every such row through it, a page at a time, to
     * hold the stored states to what the ledger of measures says they must be.
     */
    async moderationStates(afterId: string | null, limit: number): Promise<{ id: string; postId: string; moderationState: MediaRow["moderationState"]; erasedAt: Date | null }[]> {
      const found = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id, postId: postMedia.postId, moderationState: postMedia.moderationState, erasedAt: postMedia.erasedAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(and(isNotNull(postMedia.postId), afterId === null ? undefined : gt(postMedia.id, afterId)))
        .orderBy(postMedia.id)
        .limit(limit);
      return found.map((row) => ({ id: row.id, postId: row.postId!, moderationState: row.moderationState, erasedAt: row.erasedAt }));
    },

    /**
     * Deletes at most `limit` disposable rows (DISPOSABLE), the lowest ids first, inside the caller's transaction, and
     * answers the ids of the rows that are gone, in id order. The candidates are locked in id order inside the delete,
     * so the disposal and an intake's hold never lock one post's images in opposite orders; a candidate that another
     * transaction is making retained is waited for, checked again and skipped, and the batch is filled from the next ids.
     * The keep trigger decides for each row: a report that froze a candidate's post after this statement began is not
     * seen by its filter, and is seen by the trigger.
     *
     * The candidates are a materialized common table expression, which runs once. As a plain sub-select of the delete
     * they could run again for every row the delete looks at, when the planner joins the two by a nested loop: each run
     * skips the rows this statement has deleted already and lets the next ones in, so one call deleted more than its
     * limit (measured: 33 rows under a limit of 25).
     */
    async dropDisposable(tx: DbTx, limit: number): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = (await tx.execute(sql`
        with batch as materialized (
          select m.id
          from post_media m
          join profiles o on o.id = m.owner_id
          left join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
          where ${DISPOSABLE}
          order by m.id
          limit ${limit}
          for update of m)
        delete from post_media where id in (select id from batch)
        returning id`)) as unknown as { id: string }[];
      return rows.map((row) => row.id).sort();
    },

    /**
     * How many rows the disposal should have taken by now: every disposable row none of whose holds ended, and none of
     * whose marks (its own erasure, its post's deletion or erasure) was set, within the last day. A hold ends when it is
     * released or when its time passes, whichever comes first. A row whose freeze ended within the last day may be
     * counted until the next round takes it: nothing records when a freeze ends.
     */
    async overdueDeletions(): Promise<number> {
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`
        select count(*)::int as n
        from post_media m
        join profiles o on o.id = m.owner_id
        left join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where ${DISPOSABLE}
          and not exists (select 1 from media_holds h where h.media_id = m.id and least(h.released_at, h.until) > now() - interval '1 day')
          and (m.erased_at is null or m.erased_at <= now() - interval '1 day')
          and (p.deleted_at is null or p.deleted_at <= now() - interval '1 day')
          and (p.erased_at is null or p.erased_at <= now() - interval '1 day')`)) as unknown as { n: number }[];
      return row!.n;
    },
  };
}

export type MediaRepo = ReturnType<typeof createMediaRepo>;

import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { APPEALS_PAGE_SIZE, AppealsReviewedParams, DAILY_LIMITS, type AppealRequest, type AppealRow, type AppealsPage, type DecisionView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { REDRESS_VERSION } from "@korbat/rules";
import type { ActiveStaffSession, StaffStepUpConfirmed } from "../auth";
import { isDeadlock, isLockNotAvailable } from "../lib/lock-bounds";
import { authorDecisionView, decodeListCursor, encodeListCursor } from "./author";
import { reviewerOf } from "./cases";
import { ModerationError, isModerationErrorCode, type ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { recordConfirmed, refuseUnopened, subjectLockMode, type DecideOptions, type DecideOutcome } from "./decide";
import { countOrRefuse, saltedStatement } from "./intake";
import { insertAction, insertAppeal, insertReview, pendingAppeals, raisedMessage, reviewedDecision, violatedUniqueConstraint } from "./repo";

/**
 * Appeals and their reviews (3c design, sections 6.3 and 7.7). An appeal has one shape: the author's appeal of a final
 * decision that restricts them, one for each such decision, while any of its measures is in force and within six
 * calendar months of being told. A review answers that one appeal: it keeps the decision or lifts measures of it, and
 * never restricts. The database decides whether an appeal is open and who may review it; this file inserts the rows.
 */

const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * 60_000;

/**
 * The longest an appeal waits for a lock. Its trigger takes the case's row for the length of its own transaction and
 * waits for whoever holds the case: a decision that is being recorded, which for a seal over thousands of images is
 * seconds, or an erasure.
 */
const APPEAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

/** How often the appeal's transaction is run again after a deadlock or a lock timeout: in each nothing was written. */
const APPEAL_RETRIES = 2;

/**
 * POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/appeal: the author's appeal of a decision about their post or their account. In
 * this order:
 *   1. the day's limit, five for an account, counted before anything is read, so that whatever the answer the request
 *      was counted;
 *   2. one transaction that inserts the appeal's row. Its trigger decides, under a lock on the decision's case, whether
 *      an appeal of this decision is open now for this account (appeal_not_open: the decision is not a final
 *      restriction, is someone else's, is past its window, or nothing of it is in force), and the unique index refuses
 *      a second appeal (appeal_exists). The statement is optional and free of form; the server makes its salt and
 *      digest. A deadlock or a lock timeout runs the transaction again, and when the last run fails the same way the
 *      answer is service_unavailable;
 *   3. the answer: the decision as its author now reads it, with the appeal waiting. A decision that is not the
 *      viewer's, or of which they were not told, never opened by its id and does not now: not_found.
 * A request that failed through no fault of its sender gives its hit on the day's limit back.
 */
export async function fileAppeal(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "limits" | "log">, viewer: string, decisionId: string, request: AppealRequest): Promise<DecisionView> {
  const key = `appeal:day:account:${viewer}`;
  await countOrRefuse(deps, key, DAY_MS, DAILY_LIMITS.appeals);
  const statement = await saltedStatement(request.statement);
  try {
    for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
      try {
        await deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
          await tx.execute(sql`select set_config('lock_timeout', ${`${APPEAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS}ms`}::text, true)`);
          await insertAppeal(tx, { decisionId, appellantId: viewer, statement });
        });
        break;
      } catch (err) {
        const refusal = raisedMessage(err);
        if (refusal !== null && isModerationErrorCode(refusal)) throw new ModerationError(refusal);
        if (violatedUniqueConstraint(err) === "appeals_once") throw new ModerationError("appeal_exists");
        if (!isDeadlock(err) && !isLockNotAvailable(err)) throw err;
        if (attempt >= APPEAL_RETRIES) throw new ModerationError("service_unavailable", 503, undefined, 30);
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    // A refusal that is the sender's own (not open, appealed already) stays counted; anything else was not their doing.
    if (!(err instanceof ModerationError) || err.code === "service_unavailable") {
      await deps.limits.release(key).catch((failure: unknown) => deps.log.warn({ err: failure }, "appeal: a limit hit of a request that could not be saved could not be given back"));
    }
    throw err;
  }
  return authorDecisionView(deps, viewer, decisionId);
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/appeals: the pending appeals, newest first, 50 a page, each marked whether the reading person may
 * review it (3c design, section 7.7). No row carries a statement: the reviewer reads it on the case page, whose read is
 * logged and counted.
 */
export async function appealsList(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, session: ActiveStaffSession, cursor?: string): Promise<AppealsPage> {
  const after = cursor === undefined ? null : decodeListCursor(cursor);
  const found = await pendingAppeals(deps.apiDb, reviewerOf(session), after, APPEALS_PAGE_SIZE + 1);
  const page = found.slice(0, APPEALS_PAGE_SIZE);
  const last = page.at(-1);
  return {
    appeals: page.map(
      (row): AppealRow => ({
        id: row.id,
        caseId: row.caseId,
        decisionId: row.decisionId,
        filedAt: row.filedAt,
        decidedAt: row.decidedAt,
        deadline: row.deadline,
        ruleId: row.ruleId as AppealRow["ruleId"],
        legal: row.legal,
        actions: row.actions,
        reviewer: row.reviewer,
        needsAdmin: row.needsAdmin,
        mayReview: row.mayReview,
      }),
    ),
    // One row more than the page was read: only then is there a next page.
    nextCursor: found.length > APPEALS_PAGE_SIZE && last ? encodeListCursor({ at: last.sortAt, id: last.id }) : null,
  };
}

/**
 * POST /api/staff/decisions/:decision/review, once its step-up verified (3c design, section 7.7): records the answer to
 * the author's one appeal of the decision, as a decision of kind review, in the one transaction every confirmed decision
 * runs (recordConfirmed), with its audit row as appeals_reviewed on the reviewed decision.
 *
 * Before the transaction: the redress texts are those the API serves now (the rulebook version is the reviewed
 * decision's, which the database holds the review to), and the appeal the reviewer's key confirmed is the decision's
 * pending appeal: when it is not, the appeal was answered since the console read the case, and the answer is
 * case_changed with nothing written. The database forces and compares the appeal again under the case's lock, and at
 * commit holds the audit row's params to the stored review, so a review answers exactly the appeal that was confirmed.
 * It refuses a reviewer who decided anything in the case or opened a finding in it (reviewer_conflict), a party
 * (staff_recused), and a moderator where the review needs an admin (admin_required).
 *
 * After the commit the transaction's own last step does what it does for every decision: the statement's mail, the
 * count of the person's decisions, and the mail to every staff account when the review lifted a seal.
 */
export async function review(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed, ctx: { requestId: string }, options: DecideOptions = {}): Promise<DecideOutcome> {
  // A confirmation of anything else never reviews an appeal: that would be a wiring fault, not a refusal.
  if (confirmed.action !== "appeals_reviewed" || confirmed.target.type !== "decision" || confirmed.keyId !== session.keyId) {
    throw new Error("a review needs a step-up that confirmed it");
  }
  const params = AppealsReviewedParams.parse(confirmed.params);
  if (params.redressVersion !== REDRESS_VERSION) throw new ModerationError("invalid_decision");
  // The routes' one list of the kinds they accept (3e design, section 7.1 item 2).
  refuseUnopened(params, options);

  const reviewsDecisionId = confirmed.target.id;
  const reviewed = await reviewedDecision(deps.apiDb, reviewsDecisionId);
  if (!reviewed) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  if (reviewed.pendingAppealId !== params.appealId) throw new ModerationError("case_changed");
  // As for a decision: a case's target and a post's author never change, so the subject is read before the transaction.
  const subject = reviewed.target.type === "account" ? reviewed.target.id : await deps.social.postAuthor(reviewed.target.id);

  // A review holds reversals only, so its first lock stays FOR NO KEY UPDATE (3e design, section 5): a lift included.
  return recordConfirmed(
    deps,
    session,
    confirmed,
    ctx,
    subject,
    async (tx, decisionId) => {
      await insertReview(tx, { id: decisionId, caseId: reviewed.caseId, reviewsDecisionId, decidedBy: session.userId, params });
      for (const action of params.actions) await insertAction(tx, decisionId, action);
    },
    subjectLockMode(params.actions),
  );
}

/** The case a reviewed decision belongs to, for the answer to a review that has just committed. */
export async function reviewedCase(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, decisionId: string): Promise<string> {
  const reviewed = await reviewedDecision(deps.apiDb, decisionId);
  if (!reviewed) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  return reviewed.caseId;
}

/**
 * The queue and the case, for staff (3c design, section 7.3): the overview the home screen shows, the queue, the case
 * answer, the one door to a case's images, a fresh snapshot, and a moderator's own finding. Every read of a case is
 * written to the access log and counts against the day's limit; none of it needs the key.
 */

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the day, and the bands of a reporter's summary

/** How many seconds are left to midnight UTC, at least one: what a refusal at a daily limit tells the console to wait. */
export function secondsToUtcMidnight(now: Date): number {
  const midnight = Date.UTC(now.getUTCFullYear(), now.getUTCMonth(), now.getUTCDate() + 1);
  return Math.max(1, Math.ceil((midnight - now.getTime()) / 1000));
}

/** The same moment `months` calendar months later in UTC; a day the target month lacks becomes that month's last day. */
function monthsAfter(at: Date, months: number): Date {
  const month = at.getUTCMonth() + months;
  const lastDay = new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate();
  return new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), month, Math.min(at.getUTCDate(), lastDay), at.getUTCHours(), at.getUTCMinutes(), at.getUTCSeconds(), at.getUTCMilliseconds()));
}

/** A reporter's account age as a band: under one month, one to twelve months (both ends included), or over twelve. */
export function accountAgeBand(createdAt: Date, now: Date): NonNullable<SourceSummary["accountAge"]> {
  if (now.getTime() < monthsAfter(createdAt, 1).getTime()) return "under_1_month";
  return now.getTime() <= monthsAfter(createdAt, 12).getTime() ? "1_to_12_months" : "over_12_months";
}

/** How many items a reporter filed, the one being read included, as a band. */
export function itemsFiledBand(filed: number): NonNullable<SourceSummary["itemsFiled"]> {
  if (filed <= 1) return "1";
  return filed <= 9 ? "2_to_9" : "10_or_more";
}

/** The share of a reporter's decided items that were acted on, as a band; exactly half is "half or more". */
export function actedOnBand(decided: number, actedOn: number): NonNullable<SourceSummary["actedOn"]> {
  if (decided <= 0) return "none_decided";
  if (actedOn <= 0) return "none";
  return actedOn * 2 < decided ? "under_half" : "half_or_more";
}

/** How many of a reporter's items were answered while nobody could open the images, as a band; they are counted apart from the decided ones. */
export function answeredUnseenBand(unseen: number): NonNullable<SourceSummary["answeredUnseen"]> {
  if (unseen <= 0) return "none";
  if (unseen === 1) return "1";
  return unseen <= 9 ? "2_to_9" : "10_or_more";
}

/**
 * Each reporter's place among the reporters of one case, from 0, in the order of each one's first item in the case: the
 * letter the case page gives them. Given per case, so one person's letter on one case says nothing about another.
 */
export function reporterIndexes(reportersInItemOrder: readonly (string | null)[]): Map<string, number> {
  const indexes = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const reporter of reportersInItemOrder) if (reporter !== null && !indexes.has(reporter)) indexes.set(reporter, indexes.size);
  return indexes;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- recusal

/**
 * Refuses a staff account that is too close to the case's subject: every route that names a case, or an item of one,
 * asks this first, so a refused read writes no access row and does not count against the day's limit. The check never
 * looks at who reported, and its answer reads the same whoever the conflict concerns.
 */
export async function refuseRecused(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<void> {
  if (await staffCaseConflict(deps.apiDb, session.userId, caseId)) throw new ModerationError("staff_recused");
}

/** The case, after the recusal check; not_found when no case has the id. */
async function openableCase(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<CaseRow> {
  await refuseRecused(deps, session, caseId);
  const row = await caseById(deps.apiDb, caseId);
  if (!row) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  return row;
}

/** The reading person as the review marks ask about them: the session's account, and whether its role is admin. */
export const reviewerOf = (session: ActiveStaffSession) => ({ id: session.userId, admin: session.role === "admin" });

/** How long the overview's late erasures are kept before they are read again. */
export const ERASURE_OVERDUE_TTL_MS = 60_000;

/** The late erasures last read on a pool, and when: one read serves every staff member's home screen for a minute. */
const lateByPool = new WeakMap<object, { at: number; counts: Promise<ErasureOverdue> }>();

/**
 * The overview's erasureOverdue (3c design, section 7.3): one count for each due rule of what a step of the retention
 * job or the auth janitor should have changed more than a day ago and has not. The image rows are the media module's to
 * count and the notifiers' contacts the auth module's, since this module names neither.
 *
 * The counts are read at most once a minute for all staff, and a read in flight is shared: the count of late image rows
 * reads the freeze once for each kept row of a frozen account's deleted posts (seconds at twenty thousand rows), which a
 * home screen must not pay on every load, and both jobs run only every ten minutes, so a count a minute old says the
 * same. A read that failed is not kept.
 */
export function erasureOverdue(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "auth" | "now">): Promise<ErasureOverdue> {
  const now = deps.now().getTime();
  const kept = lateByPool.get(deps.apiDb);
  if (kept && now >= kept.at && now - kept.at < ERASURE_OVERDUE_TTL_MS) return kept.counts;
  const counts = (async (): Promise<ErasureOverdue> => {
    const late = await lateErasures(deps.apiDb, RETENTION);
    return { ...late, images: await deps.media.overdueDeletions(), contacts: await deps.auth.overdueContacts() };
  })();
  lateByPool.set(deps.apiDb, { at: now, counts });
  counts.catch(() => {
    if (lateByPool.get(deps.apiDb)?.counts === counts) lateByPool.delete(deps.apiDb);
  });
  return counts;
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/overview: counts, times, staff handles and cases, for every staff member's home screen. One number is
 * the reading person's own: how many of the waiting appeals they may review.
 */
export async function overview(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config" | "media" | "auth" | "now">, session: ActiveStaffSession): Promise<StaffOverview> {
  const q = deps.apiDb;
  const byLane = await openByLane(q);
  const today = await staffToday(q);
  const mails = await mailAndReleaseCounts(q, RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays);
  const appeals = await appealCounts(q, reviewerOf(session));
  return {
    lanes: ([0, 1, 2] as const).map((lane) => byLane.find((row) => row.lane === lane) ?? { lane, open: 0, oldestAt: null }),
    appealsWaiting: appeals.waiting,
    appealsYouMayReview: appeals.mayReview,
    appealsWithoutReviewer: appeals.withoutReviewer,
    reveals: await recentReveals(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    imagesToday: today.images,
    findingsToday: today.findings,
    mailsWaiting: mails.waiting,
    mailsFailed: mails.failed,
    releaseOverdue: mails.releaseOverdue,
    erasureOverdue: await erasureOverdue(deps),
    deferUnproven: deps.config.MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN === "on",
    // The three lists of the path for child sexual abuse material, which every staff member sees: what lifted the
    // protection of reported images, who chose not to seal, and which seals taken while deciding stand.
    protectionLifted: await recentProtectionLifted(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    sealsDeclined: await recentSealsDeclined(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
    interimSeals: await interimSealsInForce(q, OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the queue

const CURSOR_TIME = /^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}[.][0-9]{6}Z$/;
const CURSOR_ID = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/;

/** The queue's cursor: the last row's sort key as an opaque word. */
const encodeCursor = (row: QueueCursor): string => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify([row.lane, row.deferred, row.sortAt, row.id]), "utf8").toString("base64url");

/** Reads a cursor back; anything this module did not write is refused, never guessed at. */
function decodeCursor(cursor: string): QueueCursor {
  let parts: unknown;
  try {
    parts = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(cursor, "base64url").toString("utf8"));
  } catch {
    throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(parts) || parts.length !== 4) throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  const [lane, deferred, sortAt, id] = parts as unknown[];
  if ((lane !== 0 && lane !== 1 && lane !== 2) || typeof deferred !== "boolean" || typeof sortAt !== "string" || !CURSOR_TIME.test(sortAt) || typeof id !== "string" || !CURSOR_ID.test(id)) {
    throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  }
  return { lane, deferred, sortAt, id };
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/queue: open cases by lane and age, 50 a page. Only under the emergency switch are cases whose unanswered
 * items all come from unproven sources sorted after the others of their lane, never below a less severe lane.
 */
export async function queue(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "config">, cursor?: string): Promise<QueuePage> {
  const after = cursor === undefined ? null : decodeCursor(cursor);
  const found = await queueRows(deps.apiDb, { deferUnproven: deps.config.MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN === "on", after, limit: QUEUE_PAGE_SIZE + 1 });
  const page = found.slice(0, QUEUE_PAGE_SIZE);
  const last = page.at(-1);
  return {
    cases: page.map(
      (row): QueueRow => ({
        id: row.id,
        lane: row.lane,
        targetType: row.targetType,
        openedAt: row.openedAt,
        oldestOpenAt: row.oldestOpenAt,
        openItems: row.openItems,
        rules: row.rules as QueueRow["rules"],
        categories: row.categories as QueueRow["categories"],
        allegesIllegal: row.allegesIllegal,
        suspect: row.suspect,
        reexamination: row.reexamination,
        deferred: row.deferred,
      }),
    ),
    // One row more than the page was read: only then is there a next page.
    nextCursor: found.length > QUEUE_PAGE_SIZE && last ? encodeCursor(last) : null,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the case answer

/** A snapshot as the case answer carries it: its content unless the database's one predicate withholds it. */
function snapshotView(snapshot: SnapshotRead): CaseSnapshot {
  if (snapshot.withheld || snapshot.salt === null) return { id: snapshot.id, takenAt: snapshot.takenAt, digest: snapshot.digest, withheld: true };
  return {
    id: snapshot.id,
    takenAt: snapshot.takenAt,
    digest: snapshot.digest,
    withheld: false,
    salt: snapshot.salt,
    targetType: snapshot.targetType,
    targetId: snapshot.targetId,
    authorHandle: snapshot.authorHandle,
    postState: snapshot.postState,
    postCreatedAt: snapshot.postCreatedAt,
    replyToId: snapshot.replyToId,
    quoteOfId: snapshot.quoteOfId,
    body: snapshot.body,
    media: snapshot.media,
    displayName: snapshot.displayName,
    bio: snapshot.bio,
    handle: snapshot.handle,
  };
}

const NO_BANDS = { accountAge: null, itemsFiled: null, actedOn: null, answeredUnseen: null } as const;
const NO_CONTACT = { named: null, contactGiven: null, confirmed: null, suppressed: null, contactLost: false } as const;

/**
 * Who sent an item, as a summary that names nobody (3c design, section 7.3). A finding was found by a moderator; a notice
 * on the path for child sexual abuse material is anonymous, whoever sent it; a signed-out notifier is what the auth
 * module says of the contact, never the contact; a signed-in reporter is a letter and four bands, or, once the link to
 * the account is gone, only that.
 */
function sourceOf(item: CaseItemRow, letters: Map<string, number>, reporters: Map<string, ReporterFacts>, contacts: Map<string, NotifierFacts>, now: Date): SourceSummary {
  if (item.intakeKind === "finding") return { kind: "staff", label: SOURCE_LABELS.staff, ...NO_BANDS, ...NO_CONTACT };
  if (item.csam) return { kind: "anonymous", label: SOURCE_LABELS.anonymous, ...NO_BANDS, ...NO_CONTACT };
  if (item.channel === "signed_out") {
    const facts = item.contactId === null ? undefined : contacts.get(item.contactId);
    return {
      kind: "notifier",
      label: SOURCE_LABELS.notifier,
      ...NO_BANDS,
      named: facts?.named ?? false,
      contactGiven: facts?.contactGiven ?? false,
      confirmed: facts?.confirmed ?? false,
      suppressed: facts?.suppressed ?? false,
      // The notice left a contact that the auth module no longer has: never stored, or forgotten since.
      contactLost: item.contactId !== null && !(facts?.found ?? false),
    };
  }
  if (item.reporterAccountId === null) return { kind: "unlinked", label: SOURCE_LABELS.unlinked, ...NO_BANDS, ...NO_CONTACT };
  const facts = reporters.get(item.reporterAccountId);
  return {
    kind: "reporter",
    label: reporterLabel(letters.get(item.reporterAccountId) ?? 0),
    accountAge: facts?.createdAt ? accountAgeBand(facts.createdAt, now) : null,
    itemsFiled: itemsFiledBand(facts?.filed ?? 1),
    actedOn: actedOnBand(facts?.decided ?? 0, facts?.actedOn ?? 0),
    answeredUnseen: answeredUnseenBand(facts?.answeredUnseen ?? 0),
    ...NO_CONTACT,
  };
}

/** Whether an item's source is a signed-in reporter still linked to an account: the only items that get a letter. */
const linkedReporter = (item: CaseItemRow): string | null => (item.intakeKind === "user" && !item.csam && item.channel === "signed_in" ? item.reporterAccountId : null);

/**
 * The case as staff read it: what is, never what its senders are told (the status page keeps a live target from a dead
 * one; this answer does not). It writes nothing: readCase logs the read and holds it to the day's limit.
 */
export async function caseView(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "media" | "config" | "now">, session: ActiveStaffSession, row: CaseRow): Promise<CaseView> {
  const q = deps.apiDb;
  const origin = deps.config.APP_ORIGIN;

  // The target as it stands. An account case shows no image: a profile holds none, and the images of its posts are shown
  // only on those posts' own cases.
  let target: CaseTarget;
  let imagesAllowed = false;
  let authorId: string | null;
  if (row.targetType === "post") {
    const post = await livePost(q, row.targetId);
    target = { type: "post", id: row.targetId, link: postLink(origin, row.targetId), authorHandle: post?.authorHandle ?? null, state: post?.state ?? null, level: post?.level ?? null };
    imagesAllowed = post?.imagesAllowed ?? false;
    authorId = post?.authorId ?? null;
  } else {
    const account = await liveAccount(q, row.targetId);
    target = { type: "account", id: row.targetId, handle: account?.handle ?? null, displayName: account?.displayName ?? null, bio: account?.bio ?? null, deleted: account?.deleted ?? false };
    authorId = row.targetId;
  }

  // What the page shows in place of images on the path for child sexual abuse material: counts and days only.
  const marks = await suspicionOf(q, row.id);
  let suspicion: CaseView["suspicion"] = null;
  if (marks.holds) {
    const reach = await deps.media.reach({ type: row.targetType, id: row.targetId });
    const earlier = await earlierAnswers(q, { type: row.targetType, id: row.targetId }, authorId, SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS);
    suspicion = {
      open: marks.open,
      reach: { posts: reach.posts, images: reach.images, sealed: reach.sealed, served: reach.served, newestPostOn: reach.newestPostOn },
      // Only a post's images are ever shown in the console, so only a post's case can say when staff last looked.
      earlier: { target: { ...earlier.target, imagesOpenedOn: row.targetType === "post" ? await imagesOpenedOn(q, row.targetId) : null }, author: earlier.author },
    };
  }

  const itemRows = await caseItems(q, row.id, session.userId);
  const letters = reporterIndexes(itemRows.map(linkedReporter));
  const reporters = await reporterFacts(q, [...letters.keys()]);
  const contactIds = [...new Set(itemRows.flatMap((item) => (item.channel === "signed_out" && !item.csam && item.contactId !== null ? [item.contactId] : [])))];
  const contacts = contactIds.length === 0 ? new Map<string, NotifierFacts>() : await deps.auth.notifierFacts(contactIds);
  const now = deps.now();
  const items = itemRows.map(
    (item): CaseItem => ({
      id: item.id,
      seq: item.seq,
      position: item.position,
      createdAt: item.createdAt,
      lane: item.lane,
      // An account's address is built from the handle as it was named; the target above carries the handle it holds now.
      link: item.targetType === "post" ? postLink(origin, item.targetId) : accountLink(origin, item.namedHandle ?? ""),
      ruleId: item.ruleId as CaseItem["ruleId"],
      allegesIllegal: item.allegesIllegal,
      csam: item.csam,
      category: item.category as CaseItem["category"],
      categoryKeyword: item.categoryKeyword,
      citedLaw: item.citedLaw,
      explanation: item.explanation,
      mediaId: item.mediaId,
      suspect: item.suspect,
      // An item korbat added for a quoted post stands ten positions after the item it was added for.
      quotedByPosition: item.position > 10 ? item.position - 10 : null,
      quotedCaseId: item.quotedCaseId,
      reexaminesPosition: item.reexaminesPosition,
      reexaminesYourDecision: item.reexaminesYourDecision,
      statement: item.statement,
      outcome: item.outcome as CaseItem["outcome"],
      answeredBy: item.answeredBy,
      erased: item.erased,
      source: sourceOf(item, letters, reporters, contacts, now),
    }),
  );

  const actions = await caseActions(q, row.id);
  // The columns of 3e of every ledger row of the case, with a standing measure's period as it stands now.
  const columns = await standingColumns(q, row.id);
  // 3e Task 3: the standing measures that rest on each decision of the case, which a review or a correction would end.
  const standingOn = await standingOnDecisions(q, row.id);
  const decisions: CaseDecision[] = [];
  for (const decision of await caseDecisions(q, row.id)) {
    const own: CaseDecision["actions"] = [];
    for (const action of actions.filter((candidate) => candidate.decisionId === decision.id)) {
      const more = columns.get(action.id);
      own.push({
        id: action.id,
        kind: action.kind,
        mediaId: action.mediaId,
        noEffect: action.noEffect,
        inForce: action.inForce,
        reversesActionId: action.reversesActionId,
        liftedBy: action.liftedBy,
        // A seal's list is the database's, written when the seal was recorded: text for the report to the police.
        sealed: action.kind === "seal_media" ? await sealCovers(q, action.id, SEAL_LIST_MAX) : null,
        days: more?.days ?? null,
        announced: more?.announced ?? null,
        basis: (more?.basis ?? null) as CaseDecisionAction["basis"],
        restsOn: more?.restsOn ?? null,
        earliestStart: more?.earliestStart ?? null,
        countsUntil: more?.countsUntil ?? null,
        period: (more?.period ?? null) as CaseDecisionAction["period"],
        restedOnBy: (more?.restedOnBy ?? null) as CaseDecisionAction["restedOnBy"],
        // 3e Task 2: a retirement names the handle it retired; no other row carries the member.
        ...(more?.handle ? { handle: more.handle } : {}),
      });
    }
    decisions.push({
      id: decision.id,
      kind: decision.kind,
      outcome: decision.outcome as CaseDecision["outcome"],
      ground: decision.ground as CaseDecision["ground"],
      ruleId: decision.ruleId as CaseDecision["ruleId"],
      rulesVersion: decision.rulesVersion,
      redressVersion: decision.redressVersion,
      category: decision.category as CaseDecision["category"],
      categoryKeyword: decision.categoryKeyword,
      source: decision.source as CaseDecision["source"],
      decidedAt: decision.decidedAt,
      staffHandle: decision.staffHandle,
      throughSeq: decision.throughSeq,
      answersFromSeq: decision.answersFromSeq,
      reviewsDecisionId: decision.reviewsDecisionId,
      snapshotId: decision.snapshotId,
      suspect: decision.suspect,
      unseen: decision.unseen,
      needsAdmin: decision.needsAdmin,
      endedInterim: decision.endedInterim,
      facts: decision.facts,
      reason: decision.reason,
      legalReference: decision.legalReference,
      actions: own,
      ...(standingOn.has(decision.id) ? { standingOn: standingOn.get(decision.id)!.map((entry) => ({ kind: entry.kind, basis: entry.basis as StandingBasis })) } : {}),
    });
  }

  const texts = await caseStaffTexts(q, row.id);
  const staffText = (text: (typeof texts)[number]) => ({ id: text.id, staffHandle: text.staffHandle, createdAt: text.createdAt, text: text.text });
  return {
    id: row.id,
    lane: row.lane,
    stateVersion: row.stateVersion,
    intakeSeq: row.intakeSeq,
    answeredSeq: row.answeredSeq,
    openedAt: row.openedAt,
    closedAt: row.closedAt,
    target,
    suspicion,
    imagesAllowed,
    snapshots: (await caseSnapshots(q, row.id)).map(snapshotView),
    items,
    decisions,
    appeals: await caseAppeals(q, row.id, reviewerOf(session)),
    drafts: (await ownDrafts(q, row.id, session.userId)) as StaffTextDraft[],
    notes: texts.filter((text) => text.kind === "note").map(staffText),
    sealsDeclined: texts.filter((text) => text.kind === "seal_declined").map(staffText),
    history: (await caseHistory(q, row.id)) as CaseHistoryEntry[],
    // 3e: on a post case whether a final restriction gives a strike and its author's standing in bands (the author of a
    // post that is gone has none to show); on an account case the account's standing.
    strikeDue: row.targetType === "post" ? await strikeDue(q, row.id) : null,
    authorStanding: row.targetType === "post" && authorId !== null ? await authorStanding(q, authorId) : null,
    standing: row.targetType === "account" ? await caseStanding(q, row.id, row.targetId) : null,
  };
}

/** The alert's key for one staff account's day: its window ends at midnight UTC, so the alert goes once that day. */
const readsKey = (staffId: string) => `moderation-reads:${staffId}`;

/**
 * Tells every staff account, the person's own included, that a staff account reached the day's limit on cases: a stolen
 * key reads at the speed of requests, and this mail is how the others learn of it. Once a day for each account.
 */
async function alertDailyReads(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "limits" | "log" | "now">, staffId: string, limit: number): Promise<void> {
  const handle = (await handleOf(deps.apiDb, staffId)) ?? "unknown";
  await staffAlert(deps, readsKey(staffId), secondsToUtcMidnight(deps.now()) * 1000, { template: "moderation_reads", handle, limit });
}

/**
 * GET /api/staff/cases/:case. In this order: the recusal check; the day's limit, which counts different cases, so a case
 * the person already opened today is never refused and a reload or a decision's answer never meets it; the access row;
 * then the answer. A person at the limit is refused every other case until midnight UTC, with nothing written, and every
 * staff account is told once that day.
 */
export async function readCase(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<CaseView> {
  const row = await openableCase(deps, session, caseId);
  const limits = await dailyLimits(deps.apiDb);
  const opened = await casesOpenedToday(deps.apiDb, session.userId, caseId);
  if (!opened.thisCase && opened.cases >= limits.caseOpens) {
    deps.background.start(() => alertDailyReads(deps, session.userId, limits.caseOpens));
    throw new ModerationError("rate_limited", 429, undefined, secondsToUtcMidnight(deps.now()));
  }
  await insertAccess(deps.apiDb, { staffId: session.userId, caseId, kind: "case_opened" });
  return caseView(deps, session, row);
}

/**
 * The case as the answer to a decision the person's key has just confirmed on it (3c design, section 7.5, step 4): the
 * read is written to the access log like every read of a case, and it is not held to the day's limit on different
 * cases, which counts openings. A decision's answer is no opening of another case: its person has just acted on this
 * one, and the decision's own caps bound how often that can be. So no committed decision is answered with a refusal.
 */
export async function readDecidedCase(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<CaseView> {
  const row = await openableCase(deps, session, caseId);
  await insertAccess(deps.apiDb, { staffId: session.userId, caseId, kind: "case_opened" });
  return caseView(deps, session, row);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- images in the console

/**
 * GET /api/staff/cases/:case/media/:media/:size: an image of the case's own post, opened for staff, or image_refused. The
 * media module's one function decides what may be opened at all (gate V: never a sealed or an erased image, never an
 * image of a frozen post, on whatever case, open or closed); this route adds that the image is the case's. In this order:
 *   1. the recusal check and the case, as on every case route; only a post's case shows images;
 *   2. the image is one that a snapshot of the case lists, while that snapshot still holds its content: read from the
 *      module's own evidence, before the media module is asked. An id that names nothing and an id of another post's image
 *      are then refused by the same steps, with no file looked for, so the time an answer takes tells the two apart no
 *      more than the answer does;
 *   3. the media module's answer, and that the image it opened is on the case's own post.
 * Every refusal reads the same, and the file's handle is closed on each refusal after the open. Each view is written to
 * the access log before a byte is sent. The caller streams the file and closes it.
 */
export async function caseImage(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string, mediaId: string, size: MediaSize): Promise<StoredFile> {
  const row = await openableCase(deps, session, caseId);
  if (row.targetType !== "post") throw new ModerationError("image_refused");
  // The id in the spelling the database writes, which is the one a snapshot lists its images by.
  const imageId = mediaId.toLowerCase();
  if (!(await snapshotListsImage(deps.apiDb, caseId, imageId))) throw new ModerationError("image_refused");
  const image = await deps.media.staffImage(imageId, size);
  if (!image) throw new ModerationError("image_refused");
  try {
    // The image is of another post than this case's: the same answer as for an image that is not shown at all.
    if (image.postId !== row.targetId) throw new ModerationError("image_refused");
    await insertAccess(deps.apiDb, { staffId: session.userId, caseId, kind: "image_viewed", mediaId: imageId });
  } catch (err) {
    await image.file.handle.close();
    throw err;
  }
  return image.file;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- a fresh snapshot

/** The longest one run of the snapshot route waits for a lock: the post's row or the case's, which a decision holds while it is recorded. */
const SNAPSHOT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

/** Whether a stored snapshot holds exactly what a capture holds now. */
function sameContent(stored: SnapshotRead, live: SnapshotContent): boolean {
  const images = (list: SnapshotContent["media"]) => JSON.stringify((list ?? []).map((image) => [image.id, image.alt, image.width, image.height]));
  return (
    stored.authorHandle === live.authorHandle &&
    stored.postState === live.postState &&
    stored.postCreatedAt === live.postCreatedAt &&
    stored.replyToId === live.replyToId &&
    stored.quoteOfId === live.quoteOfId &&
    stored.body === live.body &&
    (stored.media === null) === (live.media === null) &&
    images(stored.media) === images(live.media) &&
    stored.displayName === live.displayName &&
    stored.bio === live.bio &&
    stored.handle === live.handle
  );
}

/**
 * How often the snapshot's transaction is run again after a deadlock or a lock timeout, as an intake's is: in each run
 * that gave way nothing was written.
 */
const SNAPSHOT_RETRIES = 3;

/**
 * POST /api/staff/cases/:case/snapshots: a fresh snapshot of the target as it stands, taken the intake's way (a post under
 * a share lock with its images under their row locks, held for the case; a tombstone for a deleted post; no content after
 * an erasure), when it differs from the case's newest one or that one is withheld or erased. It answers the new
 * snapshot's id and digest, or the newest one's when nothing differed, never content: the console reads the case again,
 * so every read of a case's content goes through that route's access row and the day's limit. It needs no key: it changes
 * nothing a user sees, and enters the record only through a decision that names it.
 *
 * Its locks come in another order than a decision's. An intake takes its case first, through its item; this route has no
 * row to store before the copy, and the API role, which holds no UPDATE on cases, cannot lock a case's row itself. So the
 * post is locked first, and the case's row only by the foreign key of a hold or of the snapshot's own row. A decision
 * takes the case and then its post: the two can wait for each other, and PostgreSQL then makes one give way. Like an
 * intake, the transaction is run again on a deadlock and on a lock timeout, up to three times, and when the last run
 * fails the same way the answer is case_closed: the case would not hold still, and the person tries again.
 */
export async function takeSnapshot(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "social" | "media">, session: ActiveStaffSession, caseId: string): Promise<StaffSnapshotTaken> {
  const row = await openableCase(deps, session, caseId);
  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await deps.apiDb.transaction((tx) => snapshotIn(deps, tx, row));
    } catch (err) {
      if (!isDeadlock(err) && !isLockNotAvailable(err)) throw err;
      if (attempt >= SNAPSHOT_RETRIES) throw new ModerationError("case_closed");
    }
  }
}

/** One run of the snapshot's transaction: the copy of the case's target, compared with the newest snapshot and stored when it differs. */
async function snapshotIn(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "social" | "media">, tx: DbTx, row: CaseRow): Promise<StaffSnapshotTaken> {
  const caseId = row.id;
  await tx.execute(sql`select set_config('lock_timeout', ${`${SNAPSHOT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS}ms`}::text, true)`);
  // The transaction's start, which the snapshots' trigger stamps and the digest covers.
  const takenAt = await snapshotTime(tx);
  let content: SnapshotContent;
  if (row.targetType === "post") {
    const post = await deps.social.capturePost(tx, row.targetId);
    if (!post) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
    const held = await deps.media.hold(tx, [{ caseId, postId: row.targetId }]);
    content = {
      caseId,
      targetType: "post",
      targetId: row.targetId,
      authorHandle: post.authorHandle,
      postState: post.state,
      postCreatedAt: post.createdAt.toISOString(),
      replyToId: post.replyToId,
      quoteOfId: post.quoteOfId,
      body: post.body,
      media: held.get(row.targetId) ?? [],
      displayName: null,
      bio: null,
      handle: null,
    };
  } else {
    const profile = await deps.social.captureProfile(tx, row.targetId);
    if (!profile) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
    content = {
      caseId,
      targetType: "account",
      targetId: row.targetId,
      authorHandle: profile.handle,
      postState: null,
      postCreatedAt: null,
      replyToId: null,
      quoteOfId: null,
      body: null,
      media: null,
      displayName: profile.displayName,
      bio: profile.bio,
      handle: profile.handle,
    };
  }
  const [newest] = await caseSnapshots(tx, caseId, true);
  if (newest && !newest.withheld && !newest.erased && sameContent(newest, content)) return { id: newest.id, digest: newest.digest };
  return storeSnapshot(tx, takenAt, content);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- a moderator's own finding

/**
 * POST /api/staff/findings: opens a case, or joins the target's open one, on the moderator's own finding under a rule. It
 * runs the transaction every intake runs. A finding needs no key, but it has lasting effects (holds, possibly the urgent
 * lane; citing R2 it freezes what its case reaches and makes the final decision an admin's), so one staff account opens
 * at most the day's limit of them, counted before anything is written, and the home screen lists each account's count.
 *
 * Which targets are live is the one rule of every intake: citing R2, a post in any state and an account also under a
 * handle it has left; under any other rule, only a post its author has not deleted and an account that holds the handle
 * now. A target with nothing live is not_found, and nothing is written: a finding is never stored as answered at once.
 *
 * The target is resolved first, before the day's count is read: a link that names nothing, or another site, is answered
 * as that on any day, and only a finding that could be opened meets the limit.
 */
export async function openFinding(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, request: FindingRequest): Promise<FindingResponse> {
  const { target } = request;
  let named: NamedTarget;
  if (target.kind === "post") named = { type: "post", id: target.id, mediaId: target.mediaId ?? null };
  else if (target.kind === "account") named = { type: "account", handle: target.handle };
  else {
    const parsed = parseLink(deps.config.APP_ORIGIN, target.url);
    named = parsed.type === "post" ? { type: "post", id: parsed.id, mediaId: null } : parsed;
  }
  const suspect = request.ruleId === "R2";
  const found = await liveTarget(deps, named, suspect);
  if (!found) throw new ModerationError("not_found");

  const limits = await dailyLimits(deps.apiDb);
  if ((await findingsOpenedToday(deps.apiDb, session.userId)) >= limits.findings) {
    throw new ModerationError("rate_limited", 429, undefined, secondsToUtcMidnight(deps.now()));
  }

  // A finding alleges no illegality and holds no text of its own: what the moderator writes is a saved text.
  const ground: IntakeGround = {
    kind: "finding",
    channel: "staff",
    reporterId: null,
    findingBy: session.userId,
    contactId: null,
    ruleId: request.ruleId,
    allegesIllegal: false,
    csam: false,
    category: request.category,
    categoryKeyword: null,
    citedLaw: null,
    explanation: null,
    bonaFide: false,
  };
  const live: LiveTarget = named.type === "post" ? { type: "post", id: found.id, position: 1, mediaId: named.mediaId } : { type: "account", id: found.id, position: 1, namedHandle: named.handle };
  const recorded = await recordIntake(deps, { ground, live: [live] });
  const item = recorded.items.find((candidate) => candidate.position === 1);
  if (!item || item.caseId === null) throw new Error("a finding's item was stored without a case");

  // A finding that puts an item into the urgent lane alerts staff as a notice does, after the commit and unwaited for.
  if (recorded.items.some((candidate) => candidate.caseId !== null && candidate.lane === 0)) {
    deps.background.start(async () => {
      await alertUrgentLane(deps);
    });
  }
  return { caseId: item.caseId };
}
