```ts
import { ModerationErrorCode } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db } from "@korbat/db";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { AuthForModeration } from "../auth";
import type { Config } from "../config";
import type { MediaForCases } from "../media";
import type { RateLimitStore } from "../middleware/rate-limit";
import type { SocialForModeration } from "../social";

/** The moderation codes plus the shared ones the module also raises; 3e's account_suspended is the social module's code, shared. */
export type ModerationErrorKind = ModerationErrorCode | "not_found" | "invalid_request" | "onboarding_required" | "rate_limited" | "service_unavailable" | "account_suspended";
export type ModerationErrorStatus = 400 | 403 | 404 | 409 | 422 | 429 | 503;

/** What each code answers with over HTTP (3c design, section 10). */
const STATUS: Record<ModerationErrorKind, ModerationErrorStatus> = {
  notice_link_invalid: 422,
  notice_link_offsite: 422,
  human_check_failed: 403,
  staff_cannot_report: 403,
  notice_not_found: 404,
  already_reported: 409,
  appeal_not_open: 422,
  appeal_exists: 409,
  reexamination_not_open: 422,
  reexamination_exists: 409,
  case_changed: 409,
  case_closed: 409,
  staff_recused: 403,
  staff_target: 403,
  admin_required: 403,
  reviewer_conflict: 403,
  decision_cap: 429,
  profile_changed: 409,
  snapshot_mismatch: 409,
  snapshot_erased: 409,
  text_not_found: 409,
  invalid_decision: 422,
  text_invalid: 422,
  text_quotes_user: 422,
  image_refused: 404,
  reveal_refused: 422,
  // 3e (design, section 10.5).
  reporting_restricted: 403,
  reply_not_open: 422,
  strike_mismatch: 409,
  standing_conflict: 409,
  ground_not_established: 422,
  not_found: 404,
  invalid_request: 400,
  onboarding_required: 403,
  rate_limited: 429,
  service_unavailable: 503,
  account_suspended: 403,
};

// Those of the notice routes, of the appeal and of the re-examination are written for the person reporting or reported; the
// rest for staff, whose console words them again for the screen. A recusal's words never say whether the conflict concerns the case's
// subject or someone who reported. The human check's names no contact address: the API holds none, and the
// app words that code itself.
const MESSAGES: Record<ModerationErrorKind, string> = {
  notice_link_invalid: "That link does not name a post or a profile on korbat.",
  notice_link_offsite: "Only links to this korbat can be reported.",
  human_check_failed: "We could not verify that you are human. Try again.",
  staff_cannot_report: "A staff account does not send reports. Open a finding in the staff console instead.",
  notice_not_found: "No report matches that reference and link.",
  already_reported: "You already reported this; it is being looked at.",
  // One answer for every appeal that is not open: the decision cannot be appealed, its time has passed, or nothing of it is in force.
  appeal_not_open: "This decision cannot be appealed now.",
  appeal_exists: "You have already appealed this decision.",
  reexamination_not_open: "A re-examination cannot be asked for this item now.",
  reexamination_exists: "A re-examination of this item has already been asked for.",
  case_changed: "The case changed since it was opened. Open it again.",
  case_closed: "The case changed at that moment. Try again.",
  staff_recused: "You cannot act on this case: you, or an account close to you, are a party to it.",
  staff_target: "A final decision cannot restrict a staff account. Staff are disciplined by demotion.",
  admin_required: "Only an admin can take this decision.",
  reviewer_conflict: "You cannot review this appeal: you took part in its case.",
  decision_cap: "You have reached the limit on decisions for now. Try again later.",
  profile_changed: "The profile changed since the snapshot was taken. Take a fresh snapshot and decide again.",
  snapshot_mismatch: "The snapshot is not the one this case holds.",
  snapshot_erased: "The snapshot was erased. Take a fresh one and decide again.",
  text_not_found: "A text of this decision is not saved, or was used already. Save it again.",
  invalid_decision: "This decision cannot stand as it is.",
  text_invalid: "This text cannot be saved as it is: it is too long, holds a character that cannot be kept, or does not match its digest.",
  text_quotes_user: "This text quotes what someone wrote about this case. Describe it in your own words.",
  // One answer for every image that is not shown, whatever the reason: sealed, frozen, erased, or not of this case.
  image_refused: "That image is not shown.",
  reveal_refused: "Nobody can be revealed for this item.",
  // 3e: one sentence each, for the person or for staff as the code concerns them; the console and the app word them again.
  reporting_restricted: "Your reports under korbat's rules are restricted for now. Notices of illegal content stay open to you.",
  reply_not_open: "This measure takes no reply: it has ended, was lifted, or has a reply already.",
  strike_mismatch: "The strike rule changed for this post since the case was read. Read it again and decide again.",
  standing_conflict: "A suspension or termination of this account already stands and has not ended.",
  ground_not_established: "No termination can rest on a report of images that korbat has not assessed.",
  not_found: "Not found.",
  invalid_request: "Some details are missing or invalid.",
  // The words requireSession answers with: a route with an optional session refuses such a session itself.
  onboarding_required: "Choose a handle to finish setting up your account.",
  rate_limited: "Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.",
  service_unavailable: "That could not be done right now. Try again in a moment.",
  // 3e (design, section 7.9 step 7): a report under a rule by an account whose suspension runs, in the social module's words.
  account_suspended: "Your account is suspended, so you cannot do this now.",
};

/** An expected failure of a moderation flow. The HTTP layer turns it into an ErrorEnvelope with this code and status. */
export class ModerationError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly code: ModerationErrorKind,
    readonly status: ModerationErrorStatus = STATUS[code],
    message: string = MESSAGES[code],
    /** Set for rate_limited so the response can carry Retry-After. */
    readonly retryAfterSeconds?: number,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "ModerationError";
  }
}

export function moderationErrorMessage(code: ModerationErrorKind): string {
  return MESSAGES[code];
}

/** Whether a message the database raised is one of the module's codes, which the triggers raise as their message. */
export function isModerationErrorCode(message: string): message is ModerationErrorCode {
  return ModerationErrorCode.safeParse(message).success;
}

/**
 * The work a request starts and does not wait for: the mails after a report or a notice (3c design, section 7.1, step
 * 5). The answer, which carries the reference and the token, must never wait for a relay. Every task's error is caught
 * and logged here, and the tasks are kept until they end, so that `settle` can wait for them all.
 */
export interface Background {
  start(task: () => Promise<void>): void;
  /** Resolves once every started task has ended, those started meanwhile included. */
  settle(): Promise<void>;
}

export function createBackground(log: Logger): Background {
  const running = new Set<Promise<void>>();
  return {
    start(task) {
      const run = (async () => {
        try {
          await task();
        } catch (err) {
          log.error({ err }, "moderation: a task started after a request failed");
        }
      })();
      running.add(run);
      void run.then(() => running.delete(run));
    },
    async settle() {
      while (running.size > 0) await Promise.all([...running]);
    },
  };
}

export interface ModerationDeps {
  /** The korbat_api pool. The module never sees the auth pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** The auth module's interface: the human check, a notifier's contact and every mail. The module never sees an address. */
  auth: AuthForModeration;
  /** The social module's interface: the locks on profile rows and the reads evidence is copied from. */
  social: SocialForModeration;
  /** The media module's interface: an intake's holds on image rows, which this module never names itself. */
  media: MediaForCases;
  /** The shared limit store: what one sender may send, and the throttles of the staff alerts. */
  limits: RateLimitStore;
  /** The tasks requests started and did not wait for. */
  background: Background;
  config: Config;
  log: Logger;
  now: () => Date;
}
```

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { CaseDecidedParams, MEASURE_KINDS, REVERSAL_KINDS, type ActionKind } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import type { AccountLockMode } from "../social";
import { REDRESS_VERSION, RULES_VERSION } from "@korbat/rules";
import type { ActiveStaffSession, StaffStepUpConfirmed } from "../auth";
import { boundLockWaits, isDeadlock, isLockNotAvailable } from "../lib/lock-bounds";
import { staffAlert } from "./alerts";
import { ModerationError, isModerationErrorCode, type ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { appendConfirmedAudit, caseTarget, handleOf, insertAction, insertDecision, insertMarks, raisedDetail, raisedMessage, recentDecisionsBy } from "./repo";
import { decisionStatement, sendStatement } from "./statement";

/**
 * The confirmed transaction of a decision and of a review (3c design, sections 7.5, step 3, and 7.7). The API writes
 * the decision's row, one row for each measure or reversal and, last, the audit row; the database's triggers lock,
 * check, complete and apply them (migrations 0016 and 0017), and its deferred check refuses at commit a decision whose
 * audit row does not name exactly it.
 */

/** A decision that committed, or why none did: the confirming account or key ended, or the challenge's time ran out. */
export type DecideOutcome = { decisionId: string } | "ended" | "late";

/**
 * The kinds of the ledger the decide and review routes accept (3e design, section 7.1 item 2). The params' schema knows
 * all 22 kinds from the first task of 3e on; this list holds 3c's twelve, a strike with its overruling, (Task 2) a
 * handle's retirement with its reversal and (Task 3) a suspension with its lift, and each later task of 3e adds the kinds
 * whose flow it builds, so no route records a measure whose flow is not built yet. Any other kind is refused before the
 * transaction (invalid_decision), as are a correction that keeps its decision, a non-empty list of marks and a `replaced`
 * until the tasks that open them.
 */
export const ROUTE_KINDS: ReadonlySet<ActionKind> = new Set<ActionKind>([
  ...MEASURE_KINDS.slice(0, 7),
  ...REVERSAL_KINDS.slice(0, 5),
  "strike",
  "overrule",
  "retire_handle",
  "unretire_handle",
  "suspend",
  "lift_suspension",
]);

/**
 * The order in which a decision's actions are inserted (3e design, sections 7.10 and 10.4): the signed list stays in its
 * one order (by kind, then image, so one decision has one hash), where the resets come before the retirement; the
 * database takes a retirement only as its decision's first row, so that a reset of the display name after it copies the
 * placeholder and never the retired handle. So a `retire_handle` is inserted first and the others follow in the list's
 * order. Nothing signed changes: decision_holds compares the ledger with the list as a set.
 */
export function insertionOrder<T extends { kind: ActionKind }>(actions: readonly T[]): T[] {
  return [...actions.filter((action) => action.kind === "retire_handle"), ...actions.filter((action) => action.kind !== "retire_handle")];
}

/**
 * How the module's own tests reach the database's rules below the routes: `allKinds` lifts the routes' list of kinds and
 * the outcomes and members not open yet, so that a test stores every kind of 3e as a route will once its task is built.
 * The routes never pass it.
 */
export interface DecideOptions {
  allKinds?: boolean;
}

/** The route's refusal of what it does not accept yet; nothing when the options lift the list. */
export function refuseUnopened(
  params: { actions: readonly { kind: ActionKind; announced?: boolean | null }[]; outcome: string; kind?: string; unfounded?: readonly string[]; replaced?: boolean },
  options: DecideOptions,
): void {
  if (options.allKinds) return;
  if (params.actions.some((action) => !ROUTE_KINDS.has(action.kind))) throw new ModerationError("invalid_decision");
  // The second check of the list (3e design, section 13, Task 3): a suspension is open when it is taken at once, and an
  // announced one waits for the task that builds the notice, the reply and the start.
  if (params.actions.some((action) => action.kind === "suspend" && action.announced !== false)) throw new ModerationError("invalid_decision");
  // A correction that keeps its decision answers a reply or withdraws marks: neither exists before its task.
  if (params.kind === "correction" && params.outcome === "kept") throw new ModerationError("invalid_decision");
  if ((params.unfounded ?? []).length > 0 || params.replaced === true) throw new ModerationError("invalid_decision");
}

/**
 * The lock waits one decision may meet: the subject's profile, the case, the deciding account's row, the cap's advisory
 * lock, up to three texts, the subject's account row, the post, up to four images, the key and the audit head; a review
 * meets its appeal's row in place of two of the texts. A decision that seals, lifts a seal or ends one also locks every
 * image row its seals list; that number has no bound and is not counted, and the audit row's own check of the clock
 * rolls back a transaction that outlasts the challenge.
 */
const DECISION_WAITS = 15;

/** A transaction that met a deadlock or a lock timeout is run once more only while more than this much of the challenge is left. */
const RETRY_MARGIN_MS = 60_000;

/** One staff account's decisions of the last this long are counted, and at this many every staff account is told. */
export const BURST_WINDOW_MS = 15 * 60_000;
export const BURST_ALERT_AT = 20;
/** The burst alert goes at most once in this long for one staff account, under this key of the limit store. */
export const BURST_ALERT_WINDOW_MS = 60 * 60_000;
export const burstAlertKey = (staffId: string) => `moderation-burst:${staffId}`;

/**
 * What follows a decision's commit, outside its transaction (3c design, section 7.5, step 4). Each part runs in a try of
 * its own, so none keeps another from running, and none can undo the decision:
 *   1. the author's statement is mailed when one is owed, and the result recorded; a failure of the relay leaves it
 *      pending, and the dispatch job mails it;
 *   2. the person's decisions of the last 15 minutes are counted from the decisions themselves, by the database's
 *      clock, and at 20 every staff account, the person's own included, is told, at most once an hour for one person
 *      (the throttle is a key of the limit store): a stolen key decides at the speed of key prompts, and this mail is
 *      how the others learn of it;
 *   3. a decision that lifts a seal, or a final decision on a suspicion that holds no seal (it ends a freeze without
 *      anyone having seen the images), is told to every staff account at once, without a throttle: it cannot be undone
 *      once the images are served again. A failed send is logged and not repeated; the home screen lists every such
 *      decision for 30 days.
 * A review is a decision too, and the review route starts this after its commit: its statement answers the author's
 * appeal, it counts among the reviewer's decisions, and a review that lifts a seal is told to every staff account.
 */
export async function afterDecision(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "auth" | "limits" | "log">, staffId: string, decisionId: string): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await sendStatement(deps, decisionId);
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.warn({ err, decisionId }, "moderation: a decision's statement was not mailed; it stays pending for the dispatch job");
  }
  try {
    const count = await recentDecisionsBy(deps.apiDb, staffId, BURST_WINDOW_MS);
    if (count >= BURST_ALERT_AT) {
      const handle = (await handleOf(deps.apiDb, staffId)) ?? "unknown";
      await staffAlert(deps, burstAlertKey(staffId), BURST_ALERT_WINDOW_MS, { template: "moderation_burst", handle, count });
    }
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.warn({ err, decisionId }, "moderation: a staff account's decisions could not be counted");
  }
  try {
    const found = await decisionStatement(deps.apiDb, decisionId);
    if (found) {
      const { statement, decision } = found;
      const unsealed = statement.reversals.some((reversal) => reversal.kind === "unseal_media");
      const dismissed = statement.kind === "final" && decision.suspect && !statement.measures.some((measure) => measure.kind === "seal_media");
      if (unsealed || dismissed) {
        const handle = (await handleOf(deps.apiDb, staffId)) ?? "unknown";
        const accepted = await deps.auth.mailStaff({ template: "moderation_csam_lifted", handle, at: new Date(statement.decidedAt), what: unsealed ? "unsealed" : "dismissed" });
        if (accepted === 0) deps.log.error({ decisionId }, "moderation: no staff account was mailed about a decision that lifted the protection of reported images; the home screen lists it");
      }
    }
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.error({ err, decisionId }, "moderation: the staff accounts were not told of a decision that lifted the protection of reported images; the home screen lists it");
  }
}

/**
 * The first lock a decision takes on its subject's profile row (3e design, section 5, the lock order, item 1): FOR UPDATE
 * exactly when its signed actions hold a suspension or a termination, since the ledger's trigger takes that row FOR
 * UPDATE again and an upgrade behind the case's lock deadlocks with followers' counter updates (LAB B2); FOR NO KEY UPDATE
 * for every other decision, a lift and an overruling included. (A kept answer to a reply, Task 4, joins the first.)
 */
export function subjectLockMode(actions: readonly { kind: ActionKind }[]): AccountLockMode {
  return actions.some((action) => action.kind === "suspend" || action.kind === "terminate") ? "update" : "no key update";
}

/**
 * The transaction of a confirmed decision or review, on the API's pool. In this order:
 *   1. every lock wait is bounded by a fifteenth of what is left of the challenge, at most 15 seconds; with under a
 *      millisecond left nothing is written ("late");
 *   2. the subject account's profile row in `mode` (subjectLockMode), the transaction's first lock: FOR NO KEY UPDATE, so
 *      two decisions about one account run one after the other while likes and follows of others never wait for it, or
 *      (3e) FOR UPDATE for a decision that takes a suspension, which every write of the account then waits for;
 *   3. `write`: the decision's row, whose triggers lock the case and check everything about it, and one row for each
 *      measure or reversal, in the params' order, whose triggers derive what the post and its images now are;
 *   4. last, the audit row, through public.append_confirmed_audit, on the target the key confirmed, with the params
 *      exactly as confirmed and the decision's id.
 * A deadlock, or a lock timeout the bound cut short, runs the transaction once more with the same confirmation while more
 * than a minute of the challenge is left: nothing was written, and no other request can use the spent challenge. Every
 * code a trigger raises is thrown as its ModerationError.
 *
 * Once the decision has committed, what follows it (afterDecision) is started and not waited for: the answer to the
 * person who decided never waits for a mail relay.
 */
export async function recordConfirmed(
  deps: ModerationDeps,
  session: ActiveStaffSession,
  confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed,
  ctx: { requestId: string },
  subject: string | null,
  write: (tx: DbTx, decisionId: string) => Promise<void>,
  mode: AccountLockMode = "no key update",
): Promise<DecideOutcome> {
  const action = confirmed.action;
  if (action !== "case_decided" && action !== "appeals_reviewed") throw new Error("only a decision or a review is recorded this way");
  for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      const outcome = await deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx): Promise<DecideOutcome> => {
        if (!(await boundLockWaits(tx, confirmed.expiresAt, DECISION_WAITS))) return "late";
        if (subject !== null) await deps.social.lockAccounts(tx, [subject], mode);
        const decisionId = randomUUID();
        await write(tx, decisionId);
        await appendConfirmedAudit(tx, {
          actorId: session.userId,
          keyId: confirmed.keyId,
          action,
          targetType: confirmed.target.type,
          targetId: confirmed.target.id,
          metadata: { params: confirmed.params, decisionId },
          staffSession: session.handle,
          actionHash: confirmed.actionHash,
          stepUp: confirmed.assertion,
          requestId: ctx.requestId,
          expiresAt: confirmed.expiresAt,
        });
        return { decisionId };
      });
      if (typeof outcome !== "string") deps.background.start(() => afterDecision(deps, session.userId, outcome.decisionId));
      return outcome;
    } catch (err) {
      const refusal = raisedMessage(err);
      if (refusal === "staff_confirmation_ended") return "ended";
      if (refusal === "staff_confirmation_late") return "late";
      if (refusal !== null && isModerationErrorCode(refusal)) {
        // A trigger's detail names the rule that did not hold (3e: a basis, the days, open_reports). It is logged and kept
        // on the error for the module's own tests; no answer carries it.
        const detail = raisedDetail(err);
        if (detail !== null) deps.log.info({ refusal, detail }, "moderation: a confirmed decision was refused");
        throw Object.assign(new ModerationError(refusal), { detail });
      }
      if (!isDeadlock(err) && !isLockNotAvailable(err)) throw err;
      if (attempt > 1 || confirmed.expiresAt.getTime() - deps.now().getTime() <= RETRY_MARGIN_MS) return "late";
    }
  }
}

/**
 * POST /api/staff/cases/:case/decisions, once its step-up verified: records the decision the session's key confirmed, in
 * the one transaction of recordConfirmed, with the decision's audit row as case_decided on the case.
 *
 * A seal taken while deciding stands for the reports that had arrived by the decision's time, which is its transaction's
 * start. When the only report it rests on committed while this transaction waited for its locks, the seal would be
 * recorded and not be in force: the images would stay served while the statement told their author they are sealed. The
 * database refuses such a seal itself, as its row joins the ledger (case_changed, with nothing stored); the console reads
 * the case again, and the person confirms again in a transaction that begins after the report.
 */
export async function decide(deps: ModerationDeps, session: ActiveStaffSession, confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed, ctx: { requestId: string }, options: DecideOptions = {}): Promise<DecideOutcome> {
  // A confirmation of anything else never decides a case: that would be a wiring fault, not a refusal.
  if (confirmed.action !== "case_decided" || confirmed.target.type !== "case" || confirmed.keyId !== session.keyId) {
    throw new Error("a decision needs a step-up that confirmed it");
  }
  const params = CaseDecidedParams.parse(confirmed.params);
  // A decision is made under the texts the API serves now: the redress texts always, and the rulebook unless it is a
  // correction, which carries the version of the decision it corrects.
  if (params.redressVersion !== REDRESS_VERSION || (params.kind !== "correction" && params.rulesVersion !== RULES_VERSION)) throw new ModerationError("invalid_decision");
  refuseUnopened(params, options);

  const caseId = confirmed.target.id;
  const target = await caseTarget(deps.apiDb, caseId);
  if (!target) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  // A case's target never changes, and a post's author never does, so the subject is read before the transaction.
  const subject = target.type === "account" ? target.id : await deps.social.postAuthor(target.id);

  return recordConfirmed(
    deps,
    session,
    confirmed,
    ctx,
    subject,
    async (tx, decisionId) => {
      await insertDecision(tx, { id: decisionId, caseId, decidedBy: session.userId, params });
      // The marks come after the decision's row, whose trigger answered the items, and before its measures.
      await insertMarks(tx, decisionId, params.unfounded);
      for (const action of insertionOrder(params.actions)) await insertAction(tx, decisionId, action, params.replaced);
    },
    subjectLockMode(params.actions),
  );
}
```

```ts
import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
import { RETENTION, appealDeadline, outcomeWords, type ItemOutcome, type OutcomeWordsInput } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { getRule } from "@korbat/rules";
import type { AccountMailResult, NoticeUpdateLine, NotifierUpdatePart, NotifierUpdateResult } from "../auth";
import { createJob, type JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import { MailUnavailable } from "../mail/mailer";
import { alertUrgentLane, staffAlert } from "./alerts";
import type { ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { itemLink, receiptMessage, sendReceipt } from "./intake";
import {
  beginMailRecord,
  contactsOwed,
  foldedReceipts,
  giveUpOutcomeMails,
  giveUpReceiptsAndAuthorMails,
  lockPendingOutcomeLines,
  lockPendingReceipt,
  pendingAuthorMails,
  pendingOutcomeLines,
  pendingReceipts,
  recordCarriedReceipt,
  recordOutcomeMails,
  releaseOutcomes,
  urgentItems,
  waitingCases,
  type MailState,
  type NoticeRow,
  type OutcomeLineRow,
  type UrgentItemRow,
} from "./repo";
import { sendStatement } from "./statement";

/**
 * The dispatch job (3c design, sections 7.8 and 7.12): every ten minutes it repeats the staff alerts that are still due,
 * runs the daily release once its hour has come, sends the receipts and statements a relay failure left pending, mails
 * each address and account one update of the outcomes released to it, and gives up what stayed unsent for five days.
 *
 * A round runs its steps in the order 5, 3, 1, 2, 4, 6 of the design's list: the alerts first, and the daily release,
 * which writes only to the databases, before any mail, so it never waits behind a relay. Every step runs in a try of its
 * own, and so does every mail: a failure is logged with the step and the row's id, never an address, and leaves the row
 * as it was, so a row that keeps failing never stops the alerts, the release or another row's mail. It stays pending
 * until the last step gives it up.
 *
 * Every time the job compares is its own clock's (`deps.now()`), handed to the database as a parameter, so one clock
 * decides what is fifteen minutes or five days old, and a test can move it.
 */

const MINUTE_MS = 60_000;
const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * MINUTE_MS;

/** The job's name: its lock is `job:moderation-dispatch`, and its log lines carry it. */
export const DISPATCH_JOB = "moderation-dispatch";
/** The time between the end of one round and the start of the next. */
export const DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS = 10 * MINUTE_MS;
/** A receipt, a statement and an urgent item are the job's once they are this old: until then the request that made them is still at work on them. */
const DUE_AFTER_MS = 15 * MINUTE_MS;
/** How many pending receipts one round sends. */
const RECEIPTS_PER_ROUND = 100;
/**
 * How many suspect cases one round asks the media module what they reach: one query a case, and a report of child sexual
 * abuse material needs no account, so a flood of them could hold the round's first step for minutes. The oldest cases
 * are read first; any beyond this count as calling, unread, which only repeats an alert that a case read later may ask for
 * anyway.
 */
export const URGENT_REACH_PER_ROUND = 200;
/** How long a cut-off's marker is kept: two days, so a marker is still there for every round of its own day. */
const MARKER_TTL_MS = 2 * DAY_MS;
/** How long the question "is the marker set?" holds the key when the process dies between asking and letting go. */
const MARKER_PROBE_MS = 30_000;

/** The key and the window of the queue-age alert. */
export const WAITING_ALERT_KEY = "moderation-waiting";
export const WAITING_ALERT_WINDOW_MS = DAY_MS;

/** A round's cut-off: the latest dispatch hour (UTC) at or before the round's start. */
export function cutoffOf(start: Date, hour: number): Date {
  const today = Date.UTC(start.getUTCFullYear(), start.getUTCMonth(), start.getUTCDate(), hour);
  return new Date(today <= start.getTime() ? today : today - DAY_MS);
}

/**
 * The marker of a cut-off's release, by the cut-off's day and hour. Because the key holds the hour, a changed dispatch
 * hour gives a cut-off whose release has not run. It lives beside the jobs' locks, which a restore of the database does
 * not bring back: the README's restore steps delete the markers.
 */
export const dispatchMarkerKey = (cutoff: Date) => `moderation-dispatched:${cutoff.toISOString().slice(0, 13)}`;

/** What one round did, for its log line and for the tests. */
export interface DispatchReport {
  /** The urgent lane's repeat: what became of the alert, or "none" when no item still calls for someone. */
  urgent: "sent" | "throttled" | "unsent" | "nothing_waiting" | "none";
  /** The queue-age alert: what became of it, or "none" when no case is past its time. */
  waiting: "sent" | "throttled" | "unsent" | "none";
  /** How many items the daily release changed, or null when it did not run in this round. */
  released: number | null;
  /** Whether the cut-off's release, both halves, has finished: before this round or in it. */
  marked: boolean;
  /** Whether this round ran the release to its end and wrote the cut-off's marker itself: the daily round. */
  daily: boolean;
  /** The receipts and the statements whose result this round recorded. */
  receipts: number;
  statements: number;
  /** The addresses' contacts and the accounts whose update the relay took. */
  outcomeMails: number;
  givenUp: { receipts: number; authorMails: number; outcomes: number };
}

/** What a mail's result is recorded as; nothing is recorded where the relay could not take the mail, so the next round sends it again. */
const RECORDED: Record<NotifierUpdateResult | AccountMailResult, MailState | null> = {
  sent: "sent",
  suppressed: "suppressed",
  no_address: "no_address",
  // A contact the janitor has forgotten has no address any more.
  forgotten: "no_address",
  // The relay refused the address for good: no later try changes that.
  refused: "failed",
  unavailable: null,
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 5: the alerts

/**
 * Whether an unanswered item of the urgent lane still calls for someone (3c design, section 7.12), in its three cases.
 *   1. A suspect item whose case reaches an image that is still served: until a choice not to seal is recorded on the
 *      case after the item arrived, and then only while no post with a served image was created after the newest such
 *      choice. Nothing else ends it short of the item's answer: after a note, a withhold or a field reset some reader, the
 *      uploader included, is still served the images. A seal ends it by leaving no served image.
 *   2. A suspect item whose case reaches no served image: until a decision taken while deciding, a note or a recorded
 *      choice not to seal comes after the item arrived.
 *   3. Any other item: while no decision taken while deciding came after it and, when the case is about an account or its
 *      post is not visible, no note did either. On a visible post a note never ends it: the post is withheld or decided.
 * The two times of case 1 are compared to the millisecond, and a post created in the same millisecond as the recorded
 * choice counts as created after it: the alert errs on the side of repeating.
 */
export function stillCalls(item: UrgentItemRow, reach: { served: number; newestServedAt: Date | null } | null): boolean {
  if (item.suspect) {
    if (reach === null) throw new Error("a suspect item is judged by what its case reaches");
    if (reach.served > 0) {
      if (!item.declinedAfter || item.newestDeclinedMs === null) return true;
      return reach.newestServedAt !== null && reach.newestServedAt.getTime() >= item.newestDeclinedMs;
    }
    return !(item.interimAfter || item.noteAfter || item.declinedAfter);
  }
  const noteCounts = item.targetType === "account" || item.postHidden;
  return !item.interimAfter && !(noteCounts && item.noteAfter);
}

/**
 * The open cases that hold an unanswered item of the urgent lane which is older than 15 minutes and still calls for
 * someone. What a case reaches is read once for a case, and only for a case that holds a suspect item, for at most
 * `limit` cases, the oldest first. An alert fails open: a case whose reach cannot be read counts as calling, and the
 * failure is logged with the case's id, so one case that keeps failing never silences the lane; so does a suspect case
 * beyond the limit, unread.
 */
export async function casesCalling(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "log">, now: Date, limit = URGENT_REACH_PER_ROUND): Promise<string[]> {
  const items = await urgentItems(deps.apiDb, new Date(now.getTime() - DUE_AFTER_MS));
  const reaches = new Map<string, { served: number; newestServedAt: Date | null }>();
  const calling = new Set<string>();
  // Every read counts toward the limit, one that fails too.
  let reads = 0;
  for (const item of items) {
    if (calling.has(item.caseId)) continue;
    let reach = reaches.get(item.caseId) ?? null;
    if (item.suspect && reach === null) {
      if (reads >= limit) {
        calling.add(item.caseId);
        continue;
      }
      reads++;
      try {
        reach = await deps.media.reach({ type: item.targetType, id: item.targetId });
      } catch (err) {
        deps.log.error({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "urgent", caseId: item.caseId }, "moderation-dispatch: what a case reaches could not be read; the case counts as calling");
        calling.add(item.caseId);
        continue;
      }
      reaches.set(item.caseId, reach);
    }
    if (stillCalls(item, reach)) calling.add(item.caseId);
  }
  return [...calling];
}

/** The urgent lane's repeat: while a case still calls, the alert is sent again under the key and window of the first one. */
async function repeatUrgent(deps: ModerationDeps, now: Date): Promise<DispatchReport["urgent"]> {
  if ((await casesCalling(deps, now)).length === 0) return "none";
  return alertUrgentLane(deps);
}

/**
 * The queue-age alert, at most once a day: per lane the cases past its response time with the oldest one's time, and the
 * open cases that have held a measure taken while deciding for more than a day, whose author cannot appeal it.
 */
async function alertWaiting(deps: ModerationDeps, now: Date): Promise<DispatchReport["waiting"]> {
  const waiting = await waitingCases(deps.apiDb, now);
  if (waiting.lanes.length === 0 && waiting.interim === 0) return "none";
  return staffAlert(deps, WAITING_ALERT_KEY, WAITING_ALERT_WINDOW_MS, { template: "moderation_waiting", lanes: waiting.lanes, interim: waiting.interim });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 3: the daily release

/**
 * Whether the marker is set. The lock a job runs under is also the store of its markers, and it can only take a key or
 * let it go: the question takes the key for a moment, which fails when the marker is there, and lets it go again. A
 * process that dies in between leaves the key for half a minute, not for the marker's two days.
 */
async function markerSet(lock: JobLock, key: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const probe = randomBytes(16).toString("hex");
  if (!(await lock.acquire(key, probe, MARKER_PROBE_MS))) return true;
  await lock.release(key, probe);
  return false;
}

/**
 * The daily release, until the cut-off's marker is set. (a) The database releases every item answered before the cut-off
 * and every changed outcome. (b) Every contact whose notice is still owed something is kept for another six months. The
 * marker is set once both have finished, so a round that fails in between runs the step again: the release then releases
 * nothing new, and no outcome mail goes before (b) has moved each contact's day.
 *
 * When the marker cannot be asked for, the step runs: it only repeats what a finished release leaves as it is. The round
 * is the daily one only when its own write of the marker was accepted. A marker that could not be written is logged, and
 * the next round that can write it is the daily one: a receipt that rides alone goes out once a day, never once a round.
 */
async function dailyRelease(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock, now: Date, report: DispatchReport): Promise<void> {
  const cutoff = cutoffOf(now, deps.config.MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR);
  const key = dispatchMarkerKey(cutoff);
  try {
    if (await markerSet(lock, key)) {
      report.marked = true;
      return;
    }
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.warn({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "release" }, "moderation-dispatch: the release's marker could not be read; the release runs again");
  }
  report.released = await releaseOutcomes(deps.apiDb, cutoff);
  const owed = await contactsOwed(deps.apiDb);
  if (owed.length > 0) await deps.auth.forgetNotifierAfter(owed, appealDeadline(now));
  report.marked = true;
  try {
    report.daily = await lock.acquire(key, "done", MARKER_TTL_MS);
    if (!report.daily) deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "release" }, "moderation-dispatch: the release's marker was not taken; the next round runs the release again");
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.warn({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "release" }, "moderation-dispatch: the release's marker could not be set; the next round runs the release again");
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 4: the outcome mails

/**
 * One line of the daily update, from a released item (3c design, section 7.8, step 4, and section 5). The outcome's words
 * are the contracts' one composition, with the scope the status page gives the same item; the other fields say which of
 * the mail's sentences go with the line.
 */
export function updateLine(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "config">, row: OutcomeLineRow): NoticeUpdateLine {
  const outcome = row.shownOutcome as ItemOutcome;
  const noAction = outcome === "no_violation" || outcome === "not_evident";
  let scope: OutcomeWordsInput["scope"] = null;
  // 3e (7.11 item 7): an item whose decision retired the handle reads that in place of the display name and bio, and one
  // whose decision suspended or terminated the account at once reads ACCOUNT_MEASURE_SCOPE.measure, which names nothing
  // of what the measure is or how long it lasts.
  if (row.targetType === "account") scope = row.suspect || row.sealed ? "account_suspect" : row.retired ? "account_retired" : row.measure ? "account_measure" : "account";
  else if (row.hasCase && !row.suspect && row.quotes) scope = "quote";
  // "No action for now": decided while nobody could open the post's images, on an item about a post that is not itself suspect.
  const unseen = noAction && row.decisionUnseen && row.targetType === "post" && !row.suspect;
  let rule: OutcomeWordsInput["rule"] = null;
  if (outcome === "restricted_rule") {
    // The rule in the wording of the rulebook the decision was made under.
    const found = row.ruleId === null || row.rulesVersion === null ? undefined : getRule(row.ruleId, row.rulesVersion);
    if (!found) throw new Error("the item's restriction names no rule of a rulebook korbat holds");
    rule = { id: found.id, title: found.title };
  }
  return {
    ref: row.ref,
    item: row.position,
    link: itemLink(deps, row),
    outcome: outcomeWords({ outcome, rule, suspect: row.suspect, sealed: row.sealed, unseen, noEffect: row.noEffect, scope }),
    reexamination: row.reexamines,
    changed: row.changed,
    // Only a moderator's decision to take no action can be examined again, once; an answer given with the images out of
    // sight does not spend that, also when it answered a re-examination.
    reexaminable: row.byDecision && noAction && !row.reexamined && (!row.reexamines || unseen),
    unseen,
    automatic: !row.hasCase,
  };
}

/** The log line of a mail that did not go: a relay that could not take it is expected and tried again; anything else is a fault to read. */
function logUnsent(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "log">, err: unknown, step: string, row: Record<string, string | string[]>): void {
  if (err instanceof MailUnavailable) deps.log.warn({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step, ...row }, "moderation-dispatch: a mail was not sent; it stays pending for the next round");
  else deps.log.error({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step, ...row }, "moderation-dispatch: a row failed and was left as it was; the round goes on");
}

/**
 * The outcome mails: every released item whose mail is pending, whichever round released it.
 *   - Signed out, the lines go by contact to the auth module, which alone knows which contacts share an address and sends
 *     each address one update. A receipt the 24-hour cap folded rides with its contact's lines; in the daily round a
 *     contact with a folded receipt and nothing else is passed too, so its address gets an update of receipts alone. In
 *     later rounds a folded receipt goes only with its own contact's retried lines, so an address gets one update a day.
 *   - Signed in, they go as one update per account. An item whose reporter was forgotten has nobody to mail.
 * Each line and each carried receipt records its result only while it is still pending. Where the relay could not take a
 * mail nothing is recorded, and the next round sends it again. The rows a mail's result is recorded on are taken before
 * it is sent, in the transaction that records it (beginMailRecord): a database that cannot write refuses that, and
 * nothing is sent, so a line is never mailed round after round for want of a record. The signed-out updates are one call
 * to the auth module, which groups the contacts by address, so their rows are taken and recorded in one transaction,
 * each part's record in a savepoint of its own; each account's update has a transaction of its own.
 */
async function outcomeMails(deps: ModerationDeps, report: DispatchReport): Promise<void> {
  const q = deps.apiDb;
  const rows = await pendingOutcomeLines(q);
  const folded = new Map<string, NoticeRow>((await foldedReceipts(q)).map((notice) => [notice.contactId!, notice]));

  // One part for each contact, which is one notice; one list for each account.
  const byContact = new Map<string, { ref: string; items: string[]; lines: NoticeUpdateLine[] }>();
  const byAccount = new Map<string, { items: string[]; lines: NoticeUpdateLine[] }>();
  const nobody: string[] = [];
  for (const row of rows) {
    let line: NoticeUpdateLine;
    try {
      line = updateLine(deps, row);
    } catch (err) {
      logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { itemId: row.id });
      continue;
    }
    if (row.contactId !== null) {
      const part = byContact.get(row.contactId) ?? { ref: row.ref, items: [], lines: [] };
      part.items.push(row.id);
      part.lines.push(line);
      byContact.set(row.contactId, part);
    } else if (row.reporterId !== null) {
      const update = byAccount.get(row.reporterId) ?? { items: [], lines: [] };
      update.items.push(row.id);
      update.lines.push(line);
      byAccount.set(row.reporterId, update);
    } else {
      nobody.push(row.id);
    }
  }

  // Signed out. The parts keep the order of their notices, so an address's update lists them as they were sent.
  const parts: NotifierUpdatePart[] = [];
  const carried = new Map<string, NoticeRow>();
  const withReceipt = async (contactId: string, part: { ref: string; lines: NoticeUpdateLine[] }): Promise<void> => {
    const notice = folded.get(contactId);
    if (!notice) {
      parts.push({ contactId, ref: part.ref, lines: part.lines });
      return;
    }
    try {
      const receipt = await receiptMessage(deps, notice);
      carried.set(contactId, notice);
      parts.push({ contactId, ref: part.ref, lines: part.lines, receipt: { ref: receipt.ref, receivedAt: receipt.receivedAt, items: receipt.items } });
    } catch (err) {
      // The receipt could not be built: the lines go without it, and it waits for the next daily round.
      logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { intakeId: notice.id });
      if (part.lines.length > 0) parts.push({ contactId, ref: part.ref, lines: part.lines });
    }
  };
  for (const [contactId, part] of byContact) await withReceipt(contactId, part);
  if (report.daily) {
    for (const [contactId, notice] of folded) if (!byContact.has(contactId)) await withReceipt(contactId, { ref: notice.ref, lines: [] });
  }
  if (parts.length > 0) {
    // A transaction that fails before its mail (its rows could not be taken) has sent nothing; the round goes on.
    await q.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await beginMailRecord(tx);
      // Every line's row and every carried receipt's notice, before anything is sent; what another sender recorded
      // meanwhile is left out of the mail.
      const locked = await lockPendingOutcomeLines(tx, [...byContact.values()].flatMap((part) => part.items));
      const sending: NotifierUpdatePart[] = [];
      for (const part of parts) {
        const notice = carried.get(part.contactId);
        if (notice && !(await lockPendingReceipt(tx, notice.id, true))) carried.delete(part.contactId);
        const items = byContact.get(part.contactId)?.items ?? [];
        const lines = part.lines.filter((_, index) => locked.has(items[index]!));
        const receipt = carried.has(part.contactId) ? part.receipt : undefined;
        if (lines.length > 0 || receipt) sending.push({ contactId: part.contactId, ref: part.ref, lines, ...(receipt ? { receipt } : {}) });
      }
      if (sending.length === 0) return;
      let results = new Map<string, NotifierUpdateResult>();
      try {
        results = await deps.auth.mailNotifierUpdates(sending);
      } catch (err) {
        logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { contacts: String(sending.length) });
      }
      for (const part of sending) {
        const state = RECORDED[results.get(part.contactId) ?? "unavailable"];
        if (state === null) continue;
        try {
          await tx.transaction(async (sp) => {
            await recordOutcomeMails(sp, (byContact.get(part.contactId)?.items ?? []).filter((id) => locked.has(id)), state);
            const notice = carried.get(part.contactId);
            if (notice) await recordCarriedReceipt(sp, notice.id, state);
          });
          if (state === "sent") report.outcomeMails++;
        } catch (err) {
          logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { contactId: part.contactId });
        }
      }
    }).catch((err: unknown) => logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { contacts: String(parts.length) }));
  }

  // Signed in: one update per account, through the account's own address, each in a transaction of its own.
  for (const [accountId, update] of byAccount) {
    try {
      await q.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await beginMailRecord(tx);
        const locked = await lockPendingOutcomeLines(tx, update.items);
        const lines = update.lines.filter((_, index) => locked.has(update.items[index]!));
        if (lines.length === 0) return;
        const state = RECORDED[await deps.auth.mailAccount(accountId, { template: "notice_update", lines })];
        if (state === null) return;
        await recordOutcomeMails(tx, update.items.filter((id) => locked.has(id)), state);
        if (state === "sent") report.outcomeMails++;
      });
    } catch (err) {
      // The rows are the items: the account is the reporter, whom no log line names.
      logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { itemIds: update.items });
    }
  }

  // The reporter's link was forgotten with their account: there is nobody to mail.
  if (nobody.length > 0) await recordOutcomeMails(q, nobody, "no_address");
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the round

/**
 * One round. `lock` is the store the job's own lock lives in, where the daily release keeps its markers.
 */
export async function dispatchRound(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock): Promise<DispatchReport> {
  const now = deps.now();
  const report: DispatchReport = { urgent: "none", waiting: "none", released: null, marked: false, daily: false, receipts: 0, statements: 0, outcomeMails: 0, givenUp: { receipts: 0, authorMails: 0, outcomes: 0 } };
  const step = async (name: string, run: () => Promise<void>) => {
    try {
      await run();
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: name }, "moderation-dispatch: a step failed; the round goes on");
    }
  };
  const due = new Date(now.getTime() - DUE_AFTER_MS);

  // 5. The alerts, each in a try of its own: a case whose reach cannot be read never holds the queue-age alert back.
  await step("urgent", async () => {
    report.urgent = await repeatUrgent(deps, now);
  });
  await step("waiting", async () => {
    report.waiting = await alertWaiting(deps, now);
  });

  // 3. The daily release.
  await step("release", () => dailyRelease(deps, lock, now, report));

  // 1. The receipts a relay failure left pending. sendReceipt records every result but a relay failure, which it logs
  // and leaves pending; any other fault it throws, and the row is logged here with the step and left as it was.
  await step("receipts", async () => {
    for (const intakeId of await pendingReceipts(deps.apiDb, due, RECEIPTS_PER_ROUND)) {
      try {
        const state = await sendReceipt(deps, intakeId);
        if (state !== "pending" && state !== "none") report.receipts++;
      } catch (err) {
        logUnsent(deps, err, "receipts", { intakeId });
      }
    }
  });

  // 2. The statements that were not mailed after their decision's commit, as they are mailed there.
  await step("statements", async () => {
    for (const decisionId of await pendingAuthorMails(deps.apiDb, due)) {
      try {
        if ((await sendStatement(deps, decisionId)) !== "none") report.statements++;
      } catch (err) {
        logUnsent(deps, err, "statements", { decisionId });
      }
    }
  });

  // 4. The outcome mails, only once the cut-off's release has finished, so each contact's day was moved before its lines go.
  let outcomesTried = false;
  if (report.marked) {
    await step("outcomes", async () => {
      await outcomeMails(deps, report);
      outcomesTried = true;
    });
  }

  // 6. What stayed unsent for five days is given up, without another attempt. Outcome lines only in a round that tried
  // them, after it, so each is tried at least once even when the daily release kept failing for longer than that.
  await step("give-up", async () => {
    const gone = await giveUpReceiptsAndAuthorMails(deps.apiDb, now, RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays);
    report.givenUp.receipts = gone.receipts.length;
    report.givenUp.authorMails = gone.authorMails.length;
    for (const id of gone.receipts) deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, kind: "receipt", id }, "moderation: mail given up");
    for (const id of gone.authorMails) deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, kind: "statement", id }, "moderation: mail given up");
    if (!outcomesTried) return;
    const lines = await giveUpOutcomeMails(deps.apiDb, now, RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays);
    report.givenUp.outcomes = lines.length;
    for (const id of lines) deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, kind: "outcome", id }, "moderation: mail given up");
  });

  // One line for a round that did something, so the day's release and its mails can be found in the log: counts only.
  const gaveUp = report.givenUp.receipts + report.givenUp.authorMails + report.givenUp.outcomes;
  if (report.daily || report.receipts + report.statements + report.outcomeMails + gaveUp > 0 || report.urgent === "sent" || report.waiting === "sent") {
    deps.log.info({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, ...report }, "moderation-dispatch: round");
  }
  return report;
}

/** The job: a round every ten minutes, counted from the end of the one before, on one API instance at a time. */
export function createDispatchJob(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock) {
  return createJob({ name: DISPATCH_JOB, intervalMs: DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS, lockTtlMs: DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS, lock, log: deps.log, run: () => dispatchRound(deps, lock) });
}
```

```ts
/** What the staff module needs from this one: the console's operations on cases, which its routes run behind the staff gate. */
export interface ModerationForStaff {

   * or key no longer opens anything, "late" when the challenge's time ran out; neither writes anything.

  /**

   * its own reports and notices while their records are kept, each as the account's own screens show it. Never another
   * person's report, a reporter, a notifier or a staff member.
   */
  exportFor(userId: string): Promise<ModerationExport>;
}

export interface CreateModerationOptions {
  /** The korbat_api pool. The module never sees the auth pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** The auth module's interface for moderation: auth.forModeration. */
  auth: AuthForModeration;
  /** The social module's interface for cases: socialForModeration(apiDb). */
  social: SocialForModeration;
  /** The media module's interface for cases: media.forCases. */
  media: MediaForCases;
  /**
   * The auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account with CSRF and Origin checked. The author's and the reporter's
   * routes stand behind it. Without it they refuse every request, so a module built for the staff side alone opens none.
   */
  requireSession?: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** What one sender may send, and the throttles of the staff alerts, count in the store the per-IP middleware uses. */
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  config: Config;
  logger: Logger;
  now?: () => Date;

export function createModeration(options: CreateModerationOptions) {
  const deps: ModerationDeps = {
    apiDb: options.apiDb,
    auth: options.auth,
    social: options.social,
    media: options.media,
    limits: options.rateLimitStore,
    background: createBackground(options.logger),
    config: options.config,
    log: options.logger,
    now: options.now ?? (() => new Date()),
  };
  const forStaff: ModerationForStaff = {
    decide: (session, confirmed, ctx) => decide(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
    decidedCase: (session, caseId) => readDecidedCase(deps, session, caseId),
    review: (session, confirmed, ctx) => review(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
    reviewedCase: async (session, decisionId) => readDecidedCase(deps, session, await reviewedCase(deps, decisionId)),
    appeals: (session, cursor) => appealsList(deps, session, cursor),
    overview: (session) => overview(deps, session),
    queue: (cursor) => queue(deps, cursor),
    caseView: (session, caseId) => readCase(deps, session, caseId),
    caseImage: (session, caseId, mediaId, size) => caseImage(deps, session, caseId, mediaId, size),
    takeSnapshot: (session, caseId) => takeSnapshot(deps, session, caseId),
    openFinding: (session, request) => openFinding(deps, session, request),
    saveText: (session, caseId, request) => saveText(deps, session, caseId, request),
    texts: (session, caseId) => ownTexts(deps, session, caseId),
    reveal: (session, confirmed, ctx) => reveal(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
  };
  const forSocial: ModerationForSocial = {
    authorFacts: (viewer, postIds) => authorFacts(deps, viewer, postIds),
  };
  const forAccount: ModerationForAccount = {
    forgetAccount: async (userId) => {
      await forgetReporter(deps.apiDb, userId);
    },
    exportFor: (userId) => exportFor(deps, userId),
  };
  return {
    deps,
    /**
     * The app's routes, mounted at /api: reports and notices, their status page with its contact buttons and its
     * re-examinations, and behind the session guard the account's own decisions, appeals, reports and re-examinations.
     */
    routes: moderationRoutes(deps, options.requireSession ?? noSession),
    /** The interface the staff module uses. */
    forStaff,
    /** The interface the social module's views use. */
    forSocial,
    /** The interface the account module's purge and export use. */
    forAccount,
    /**
     * 3e (design, section 7.12): /api/me's standing, read fresh from the ledger: null for an account without a live
     * profile. The app composes the route from this and the auth module's meFor.
     */
    standingFor: (userId: string) => standingFor(deps.apiDb, userId),
    /**
     * Resolves once every task a request started and did not wait for has ended: the mails after a report, a notice, a
     * finding, a reveal or a refused case read. The tests await it; the server lets the tasks run.
     */
    settle: () => deps.background.settle(),
    /**
     * Starts the module's background work under the jobs' shared lock, on one API instance at a time: the dispatch job
     * always, and the retention job only while MODERATION_RETENTION is on. Each one's first round comes ten minutes after
     * the start. While the switch is off nothing is erased, released or deleted, and the warning is logged at every start,
     * so a switch left off after a restore is seen. Answers the function that stops both; a round in flight finishes.
     */
    startJobs: (lock: JobLock): (() => void) => {
      const stopDispatch = createDispatchJob(deps, lock).start();
      if (deps.config.MODERATION_RETENTION !== "on") {
        deps.log.warn(RETENTION_OFF_WARNING);
        return stopDispatch;
      }
      const stopRetention = createRetentionJob(deps, lock).start();
      return () => {
        stopDispatch();
        stopRetention();
      };
    },
  };
}

export type Moderation = ReturnType<typeof createModeration>;
```

```ts
/**

 * target it names, each item in exactly one open case, and the first copy of each target as evidence. First the
 * transaction every intake runs (step 4); below it what a report or a notice passes before it and what follows its
 * commit (steps 1 to 3, 5 and 6), and the notifier's status page and contact (section 7.2).
 */

/** What an intake alleges and who sent it: the ground's columns of the intake's row. */
export interface IntakeGround {
  kind: "user" | "finding";
  channel: "signed_in" | "signed_out" | "staff";
  /** The signed-in reporter; never set on the path for child sexual abuse material, which records no sender. */

/** For a target of a re-examination: the item that is examined again, and what its sender added to the request. */
export type Reexamines = NonNullable<ItemRow["reexamines"]>;

/**

 * place among the targets named, from 1. With `reexamines` its item is a re-examination, which takes its position from
 * the item it examines again.
 */
export type LiveTarget =
  | { type: "post"; id: string; position: number; mediaId?: string | null; reexamines?: Reexamines }
  | { type: "account"; id: string; position: number; namedHandle: string; reexamines?: Reexamines };

/** A target with nothing live: a link to a post that names no row or a deleted one, or a handle that names no account. It is stored as answered at once. */
export type DeadTarget = { type: "post"; id: string; position: number; reexamines?: Reexamines } | { type: "account"; position: number; namedHandle: string; reexamines?: Reexamines };

export interface IntakeRequest {
  ground: IntakeGround;
  live: readonly LiveTarget[];
  dead?: readonly DeadTarget[];
}

export interface RecordedItem {
  id: string;
  position: number;

  token: string | null;
  /** Whether the intake's items are suspect: it is on the CSAM path, or a finding citing R2. */
  suspect: boolean;
  items: RecordedItem[];

/** How often the transaction is run again after a case closed under it, a deadlock or a lock timeout: in each nothing was written. */
const RETRIES = 3;
/** How often one transaction asks for a target's open case before it starts over. */
const CASE_READS = 3;
/**
 * The longest the intake waits for a lock. A case's row is held by a decision for as long as that decision's
 * transaction runs, which for a seal over thousands of images is seconds; an intake that waited longer starts over.
 */
const LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

const BASE32 = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ234567";

/** A fresh public reference: N- and ten base32 characters from 50 random bits. */
function newRef(): string {
  const bytes = randomBytes(7);
  // 48 bits and two more: 50 in all, which a JavaScript number holds exactly.
  const bits = bytes.readUIntBE(0, 6) * 4 + (bytes[6]! & 3);
  let ref = "";
  // 50 bits, five at a time from the top.
  for (let shift = 45; shift >= 0; shift -= 5) ref += BASE32[Math.floor(bits / 2 ** shift) % 32];
  return `N-${ref}`;
}

/** Whether an intake's items are suspect, as the attach trigger forces it: the CSAM path, or a finding citing R2. */
export const isSuspect = (ground: IntakeGround) => ground.csam || ground.ruleId === "R2";

/**
 * The live targets of a suspect intake with the items korbat adds: a post's card shows the images of the post it
 * quotes, so a report of child sexual abuse material about a post that quotes another is a report about both. Each
 * quoted post that the request does not name itself becomes a target of its own, at the position of the item it was
 * added for plus 10 (the lowest such position when several named posts quote it). One level only, as a card draws one
 * quote deep: an added target brings none of its own. Read outside any transaction; a post's quote never changes.
 */
export async function withAddedTargets(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "social">, live: readonly LiveTarget[]): Promise<LiveTarget[]> {
  const named = new Set(live.filter((target) => target.type === "post").map((target) => target.id));
  const added = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const target of live) {
    if (target.type !== "post" || target.position > 10) continue;
    const quoted = (await deps.social.postRef(target.id))?.quoteOfId;
    if (!quoted || named.has(quoted)) continue;
    added.set(quoted, Math.min(added.get(quoted) ?? target.position, target.position));
  }
  return [...live, ...[...added].map(([id, position]): LiveTarget => ({ type: "post", id, position: position + 10 }))];
}

/** Thrown inside the transaction to roll it back and run it again: the case a target was read into closed before the read found one. */
class StartOver extends Error {}

/** A case's targets in one order for every intake: by kind (posts before accounts, as the database orders the two) and then by id. */
const byTarget = (a: LiveTarget, b: LiveTarget) => (a.type !== b.type ? (a.type === "post" ? -1 : 1) : a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0);

/**
 * Stores one intake in one transaction, which changes nothing unless it commits. In this order:
 *   1. a signed-in reporter's profile row, FOR KEY SHARE, refusing a missing or deleted account;
 *   2. the intake's row, with a fresh reference and, for a signed-out or CSAM notice, the hash of a fresh token;
 *   3. for each live target, in the targets' order: its open case (opened when there is none) and then its item, which
 *      the attach trigger numbers into the case, so every intake takes its cases in one order and two notices that name
 *      the same targets never deadlock; only then the captures, posts in id order, each under a share lock on its post,
 *      so none holds a post while it waits for a case;
 *   4. one hold through the media module for the whole intake: the image rows of every post target, and for a suspect
 *      item about an account every image row on the account's posts, locked by one statement in one id order, with each
 *      post's case's evidence hold on its images; then a snapshot for each case that holds none yet, or, for an account,
 *      whose newest one differs from the account now, a post's listing the images the hold answered;
 *   5. for each target with nothing live, an item with no case, answered at once.
 * It is run again, up to three times, when an item's case closed in between (the attach trigger says so), on a deadlock
 * and on a lock timeout; when the last run fails the same way the answer is case_closed. A signed-in reporter who already
 * has an item on the same ground in a target's open case is answered already_reported.
 */
export async function recordIntake(deps: ModerationDeps, request: IntakeRequest): Promise<IntakeRecorded> {
  const suspect = isSuspect(request.ground);
  const live = suspect ? await withAddedTargets(deps, request.live) : [...request.live];
  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
    try {
      return await deps.apiDb.transaction((tx) => recordIn(deps, tx, { ...request, live }, suspect));
    } catch (err) {
      const constraint = violatedUniqueConstraint(err);
      if (constraint === "intake_items_reporter_once") throw new ModerationError("already_reported");
      // A reference another intake already has: one in 2^50 for each pair. The next run draws a new one.
      const startOver = err instanceof StartOver || isSerializationFailure(err) || isDeadlock(err) || isLockNotAvailable(err) || constraint === "intakes_ref_unique";
      if (!startOver) throw err;
      if (attempt >= RETRIES) throw new ModerationError("case_closed");
    }
```
